entry.title: Tight limits on online selection with downward-closed constraints
entry.summary: Tight Bounds for Downward-Closed Prophet and Secretary Problems arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies online selection problems under arbitrary downward-closed feasibility constraints, considering different arrival orders and distributional assumptions. It establishes bounds for the standard adversarial-order prophet problem, the Bayesian random-order prophet secretary problem (and by extension the standard secretary problem), and the free-order prophet problem. Combined with earlier complementary results, these bounds pin down the asymptotically tight competitive ratios for these variants. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give tight competitive-ratio bounds for downward-closed prophet and secretary problems across several arrival orders, reporting a superconstant separation between random-order and free-ord

entry.title: Universal optimality on finite Lee tori: which equal-size point sets minimize pair energy on finite Lee tori for all potentials of a given class.
entry.summary: Universal optimality on finite Lee tori arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies subsets of finite Lee tori that minimize pair energy among sets of the same size, for every discretely completely monotone potential. At half occupancy on a product of even cycles, the two checkerboard sets minimize both total and maximum individual energy, and they are the only minimizers for nonconstant classical completely monotone potentials, proving the checkerboard conjecture for this class. The paper also characterizes when universally optimal sets exist at the independence number and gives a characterization at density 1/5 in Z_5^n via weighted counts of pairs at distances one and two. The proofs use integer box occupancy bounds and Fourier certificates. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize universally optimal sets on finite Lee tori, prove the checkerboard conjecture for classical completely monotone potentials, and identify universally optimal sets in several Z

entry.title: Proves that checking membership in the tournament equilibrium set is PSPACE-complete
entry.summary: The Tournament Equilibrium Set Is PSPACE-Complete, Even under Hereditary Uniqueness arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies the tournament equilibrium set (TEQ), a voting rule proposed by Schwartz in 1990 that relies on pairwise majority comparisons and is defined recursively. It proves that deciding whether a given alternative belongs to TEQ is PSPACE-complete, closing the gap between the previously known NP-hardness and PSPACE membership. The hardness holds even when every nonempty subtournament has a unique minimal retentive set. The paper also shows how the complexity changes with the bound on the number of dominators. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove TEQ membership is PSPACE-complete, even under hereditary uniqueness, and give a fuller dominator-bound complexity classification for tournament solutions.

entry.title: Submodular secretary problem: tight 1-1/e for monotone objectives, and a ratio strictly between 1/e and 1/2 in general
entry.summary: The Submodular Secretary Problem: Tight 1-1/e for Monotone Objectives, and Strictly Between 1/e and 1/2 in General arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper studies the submodular secretary problem with a cardinality constraint, where elements arrive in random order and must be accepted or rejected irrevocably to maximize a nonnegative submodular function over sets of at most k elements. For monotone objectives, the optimal competitive ratio tends to exactly 1-1/e as k grows, achieved by an algorithm using at most 4n+1 value queries. For general objectives, the optimal limiting ratio is shown to lie strictly between 1/e and 1/2, using a new technique called eligibility attenuation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a tight 1-1/e ratio for monotone objectives with one algorithm, and improve general objectives to a value strictly between 1/e and 1/2 via eligibility attenuation.

entry.title: Fictitious play for agents using nonlinear risk-based evaluation in 2×2 games
entry.summary: Fictitious Play When Agents Are Not Expected-Utility Maximizers: A Geometric Analysis in 2-Action Games arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies nonlinear fictitious play, where agents evaluate each action with a possibly nonlinear functional of the opponent's payoff distribution rather than maximizing expected payoff. The authors identify a single-crossing property that preserves the classical geometry of fictitious play in 2×2 games and analyze convergence geometrically even when this property fails. They show that in a 2×3 game, convergence can fail even in continuous time when the two-action player uses conditional value-at-risk. They also give a finite-crossing condition that ensures convergence in general 2×n games.

entry.title: "Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete" — a proof that deciding a forced win in the sowing game Kalah is PSPACE-complete as board size grows
entry.summary: Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies Kalah, a classic two-player sowing game in the mancala family, with the number of pits per side treated as part of the input. It shows that deciding whether a designated player can force a win from an arbitrary position is PSPACE-complete. The proof introduces an intermediate game, Line Kalah, reduces quantified Boolean formulas to it, and embeds the line positions into Kalah with both stores empty. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that deciding forced wins in generalized Kalah is PSPACE-complete via a reduction from QBF through an intermediate Line Kalah problem, valid under both capture conventions and bonus

entry.title: PACER: Managing GPU Power Overshoots for Machine Learning Workloads
entry.summary: PACER: GPU Excursion Management for ML Workloads arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper examines intra-GPU performance variability caused by brief power excursions, which occur when GPU power temporarily exceeds its rated limits. The authors are the first to characterize how large and how frequent these overshoots are, finding them especially common in machine learning workloads with short, power-hungry kernels. They design hardware and firmware mechanisms to make power management more consistent and reduce this variability. Across popular workloads, the approach improves performance by 3-12% over state-of-the-art GPU power management and comes within 3% of an oracular solution.

entry.title: Learning dynamics of a spatial game on resource landscapes
entry.summary: Learning Dynamics of the Influencer's Game in Resource Landscapes arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper introduces the influencer's game, a spatial game in which players occupy positions in a trait space and receive shares of resources based on their relative influence at each trait point. The authors show that a unique symmetric Nash equilibrium exists when the influence kernel is strictly log-concave, and they analyze how stability depends on kernel parameters, player count, and resource distribution shape. Beyond the equilibrium analysis, the paper identifies stability thresholds and bifurcation types, and it supports the results with real-world resource data and multi-agent reinforcement learning experiments. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a new spatial game, prove a unique symmetric equilibrium, derive a stability threshold and bifurcations, and test with real data and reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Broadcast Instead of Copying: Removing Weight HBM from Datacenter LLM Inference
entry.summary: Broadcast, Don't Replicate: Eliminating Weight HBM in Datacenter LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper proposes Optical Broadcast Memory (OBM), a hierarchical fiber architecture that replaces an earlier optical fiber loop memory design for serving large language models. A central memory server continuously broadcasts model weights, and inference nodes passively tap the data stream using receive-only co-packaged optics. Evaluated at 80,000 accelerators, the approach eliminates petabytes of HBM while matching or exceeding an HBM-based system in throughput and energy per token.

entry.title: Locality and Interference in Radio Multicasting: Structure and Scheduling
entry.summary: Locality Meets Interference: Structure and Scheduling in Radio Multicasting arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies multipoint-to-multipoint multicasting in synchronous radio networks where participant locations are unknown and messages can be freely aggregated. It gives completion-time bounds for several schedules, including ones based on distance-two coloring, geometric data in unit disk graphs, strong selectivity, and random transmission. For one-hop designated delivery, it proves that the optimal schedule length equals the chromatic number of a conflict graph and is at most 2b−1.

entry.title: Explicit codes correcting insertions, deletions, and substitutions via multicoloring
entry.summary: Explicit Edit Codes via Multicoloring arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper constructs explicit q-ary codes of length n that correct any combination of at most t insertions, deletions, and substitutions. Their redundancy is 2t·log_q n plus O(log log n) q-ary symbols, matching the leading term of Levenshtein's classical existential bound. The approach uses a prime-based multicoloring of the edit-confusion graph, and the construction supports deterministic encoding and decoding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use prime-based multicoloring of the edit-confusion graph to match Levenshtein's leading redundancy term 2t log_q n, with deterministic encoding and decoding time bounds.

entry.title: Information spectrum methods for multiple-access channels, Part III: strong converse for the K-user Gaussian case
entry.summary: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the K-User Gaussian Case arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This is Part III of a series on K-user multiple-access channels. Starting from two fundamental lemmas, the authors derive the capacity region of the general K-user MAC with cost constraints and show it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the K-user Gaussian MAC. Using an information spectrum calculation, they prove that rate tuples outside the capacity region yield error probabilities tending to one, establishing the strong converse. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan.

entry.title: Capacity limits for multi-user channels that stay fixed during each codeword
entry.summary: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : ǎrepsilon-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies the ε-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels with finite alphabets, where the channel law stays fixed across a codeword, as in a slowly fading link. The authors derive a single-letter inner bound and an outer bound called the outage region, and show that the two coincide for well-ordered mixed MACs. They also extend Ahlswede's strong converse to K users.

entry.title: Autonomous Mobile Robots on a Computing Field: a model where the floor itself computes
entry.summary: Autonomous Mobile Robots on a Computing Field arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper introduces CABOT, a model in which the discrete plane robots move on is an active cellular automaton rather than a passive stage. The robots are deliberately weak, seeing only nearby cell states and robot positions, so the number of floor states becomes the measure of required resources. The authors show that a handful of states enables line formation, gathering and exploration, and prove that gathering and line formation cannot be solved when the floor must stay silent. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast the grid floor as a cellular automaton, reporting solvability and impossibility results for line formation, gathering and exploration with few states.

entry.title: An optimized Mirabbasi-Martin pulse shaping filter for higher-order modulation in Zak-OTFS
entry.summary: Optimized Mirabbasi-Martin Pulse Shaping Filter for Higher-Order Modulation in Zak-OTFS arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a separable two-dimensional Mirabbasi-Martin (MM) filter for Zak-OTFS modulation, together with a coefficient optimization method that minimizes aggregate sidelobe energy while keeping a compact structure. The optimized filter has no sidelobes and the narrowest -40 dB delay-Doppler pulsewidth among the compared sinc, Gaussian, and GS pulses, which confines pilot energy and reduces pilot-data interference. Simulations show better uncoded and coded bit error rate for higher-order QAM than these alternative filters.

entry.title: Regime-Uncertain Data Transactions: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Self-Adapting Multi-ML-Agent Systems
entry.summary: Regime-Uncertain Data Transactions: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Self-Adapting and Self-Diagnosing Multi-ML-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies how autonomous ML agents in large organizations exchange data across legal boundaries when the applicable rules are uncertain. It models each exchange as a game between two agents and an enforcer, where agents hold beliefs about which rules apply and bargain over legal bundles using a method called LCNB. In a synthetic simulator covering GDPR, DPDP, CCPA/CPRA and a stricter regime, a citizenship-based rule violated 21–37% of shared records in two of three stress cases, while LCNB violated under 1%. The authors note limits, including that under default settings LCNB shares mostly aggregates, which partly explains its low violation rate.

entry.title: SS-HSDP: Faster, More Flexible Sharded Training by Decoupling Runtime and Update Parameters
entry.summary: SS-HSDP: Efficient and Flexible Sharded Data Parallelism via Runtime-Update Decoupling arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents SS-HSDP, a training framework that separates runtime parameters from update parameters so that computation layouts and optimization units can be organized independently. Using shared data views and hierarchical sharding, it avoids redundant data movement and supports optimizers such as Muon, along with fully zero-copy execution. In experiments on video and language model training with MXFP8, it achieves higher Model FLOPs Utilization than FSDP2, veScale-FSDP, and Megatron-FSDP. At 128 GPUs, MFU improves by up to 21.7% over the fastest baseline, with comparable or lower peak memory.

entry.title: Linear-order improvement of the Gilbert-Varshamov bound for linear and quantum codes
entry.summary: A Theta(n)-Multiplicative Improvement of the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound for Linear and Quantum Codes arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper concerns the Gilbert-Varshamov bound, a standard benchmark for the existence of error-correcting codes. For q-ary linear codes, the best previously known general improvement was of order Θ(√n). The authors use a new viewpoint that tolerates O(n) low-weight points and removes them together at the cost of one dimension, yielding a Θ(n) multiplicative improvement for linear codes of arbitrary rate. The method is also extended to quantum codes, giving a Θ(n) improvement of the quantum GV bound for a stated range of relative distances. ★★★★ Notable: The authors achieve a Θ(n)-multiplicative GV improvement for linear codes by allowing O(n) low-weight points and eliminating them jointly, extended to quantum codes.

entry.title: Flexible metasurfaces that reshape the array to improve secure wireless transmission
entry.summary: Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces for Enhancing Secure MISO Communications arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies secure wireless transmission from a multi-antenna transmitter to one receiver in the presence of a multi-antenna eavesdropper, using a flexible intelligent metasurface whose shape can be changed. The transmit covariance matrix and the surface shape are jointly optimized to maximize secrecy rate, using a block coordinate ascent algorithm. Numerical results show higher secrecy rate than a conventional rigid antenna array, with about 2.5 dB transmit-power saving at the same secrecy rate.

entry.title: Strategically Robust Multi-Agent Control: A New Equilibrium Between Game-Theoretic and Robust Control
entry.summary: Strategically Robust Multi-Agent Control arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces strategically robust multi-agent control, which fills the gap between game-theoretic control and robust control. In dynamic games, players seek protection against misspecified control policies of other players, leading to a new equilibrium concept called strategically robust dynamic equilibrium. The authors study this concept in canonical open- and closed-loop settings. Numerical experiments on vehicle platooning, inventory management, and network control show resilience to misspecification and cases where strategic robustness improves performance or social welfare.

entry.title: Snoopie: A Multi-GPU Communication Profiler and Visualizer
entry.summary: Snoopie: A Multi-GPU Communication Profiler and Visualizer arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents Snoopie, a profiling tool for multi-GPU systems that tracks peer-to-peer GPU data transfers and calls from GPU-centric communication libraries. It attributes data movement to source code lines and data objects, and offers visualizations from system-wide views down to specific instructions and addresses. Case studies show its use in monitoring data movement, finding performance bugs, and understanding transfers hidden beneath communication libraries. The tool is publicly available.

entry.title: Designing Information in a Forest: Algorithmic Aspects
entry.summary: Designing Information in a Forest: Algorithmic Aspects arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies Bayesian persuasion where a sender reveals information to multiple receivers whose information hierarchy is a pre-specified directed forest. Using a binary state and binary actions, it extends a tractability result for symmetric sender utility from private persuasion to the forest setting and gives a polynomial-time algorithm for modular utility. For supermodular utility, the problem is shown to be NP-hard with no FPTAS unless P=NP, and an approximation algorithm whose ratio depends linearly on the forest depth is provided.

entry.title: Smoothed Analysis for Distributed Maximal Independent Set
entry.summary: Smoothed Analysis for Distributed MIS arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies smoothed analysis of the distributed Maximal Independent Set (MIS) problem, where each edge of an arbitrary base graph is independently toggled with probability p. When p is about β·ln n/n for a large constant β, a randomized LOCAL algorithm computes an MIS in O(√log n) rounds with high probability, beating the worst-case lower bound. Conversely, for p at most (1/2−δ)·ln n/n, some base graph forces every randomized LOCAL algorithm to need Ω(log n/log log n) rounds, so the smoothing required is optimal up to a constant factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply smoothed analysis to distributed MIS, reporting O(√log n)-round randomized LOCAL algorithms and a nearly tight matching lower bound.

entry.title: Parallel computing systems for choosing the optimal process equipment
entry.summary: Parallel Computing Systems for the Optimal Selection of Process Equipment arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This monograph studies how to select equipment for multiproduct batch chemical plants, a large NP-hard optimization problem that minimizes total capital cost while keeping the plant operable. The authors develop a branch-and-bound algorithm and parallel versions for shared-memory, cluster, and GPU systems. They also propose a hybrid method combining Ant Colony Optimization and Simulated Annealing, implemented on GPUs. Experiments report that the parallel hybrid algorithm finds solutions within 0.01% of the branch-and-bound optimum in tens of seconds, compared with tens of hours.

entry.title: A constructive theory for closed-form rate-distortion functions (methods for deriving exact formulas of rate-distortion functions)
entry.summary: A Constructive Theory of Closed-Form Rate-Distortion Functions arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper develops a posterior-based construction framework for rate-distortion functions, using conditional entropy as a common distortion coordinate. It proves entropy-level attainability for finite-alphabet discrete sources and for absolutely continuous sources with integrable log densities, via constructive rate-entropy coding. The authors derive exact expressions for several source models, including Gamma, zeta, and negative binomial sources under specified distortion measures and intervals.

entry.title: MegaOps: A Kernel Overlapping Framework Combining PyTorch-style Modularity with Megakernel Speed
entry.summary: MegaOps: A Kernel Overlapping Framework with PyTorch-like Modularity and Megakernel Performance arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper presents MegaOps, a framework that keeps the one-GPU-kernel-per-operator design of PyTorch-style ML frameworks while removing barriers between dependent kernels. Instead of fusing operators into a single megakernel, it runs dependent kernels on separate CUDA streams and synchronizes them on individual tiles of the intermediate tensor. Evaluated on dense Llama3 and Qwen3 models across H100, A100, and L40 GPUs and multi-GPU servers, MegaOps matches hand-tuned ThunderKittens megakernel throughput. It reaches 1.09 to 1.10 times the best baseline's decode throughput and 0.98 to 1.10 times its prefill throughput. ★★★★ Notable: The authors remove kernel barriers via tile-level dependencies without fusing kernels, reporting parity with ThunderKittens megakernels and 1.09-1.10x decode throughput on Llama3 and Qwen3.

entry.title: Core nonemptiness for 2/3-convex games: whether a relaxed class of cooperative games always has a stable payoff allocation
entry.summary: Core nonemptiness for 2/3-convex games arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies the core of 2/3-convex games, a generalization of convex games in which at least two of any three distinct coalitions satisfy the supermodular inequality. It shows that every such game has a marginal worth vector in the core, so the core is nonempty, and the proof is constructive, yielding a linear-time algorithm for a core allocation. The authors also examine how 2/3-convexity relates to permutational convexity and introduce a model based on the OSCE's consensus-minus-two procedure, showing it is 2/3-convex but not necessarily convex.

entry.title: Faster Serverless LLM Cold Starts Through Shared and Prewarmed Startup Work
entry.summary: Fast Serverless LLM Cold Starts by Sharing and Prewarming Startup Work arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper observes that serverless LLM cold starts take about a minute, with only 5-11% spent loading weights and most time going to repeated compilation, memory profiling and runtime setup. It presents Cairn, which lets the first server publish weights and engine artifacts to a CXL memory pool shared across the cluster, so other servers read them in place, and completes model-independent setup ahead of time in warm containers. Using ServerlessLLM on vLLM v0.20 with six models from 1B to 14B and an emulated shared CXL pool, Cairn reports 4.1-5.2x faster cold starts on servers without their own checkpoint and a 64% reduction in median TTFT.

entry.title: Concatenated codes with one inner code achieving low-rate Gilbert-Varshamov distance
entry.summary: Concatenated Codes with One Inner Code: Low-Rate Gilbert-Varshamov Asymptotics from Algebraic-Geometric Codes arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies concatenated codes that use one binary inner code for all outer coordinates, with outer codes taken as random subcodes of scaled algebraic codes. It gives a general upper bound on the probability that the minimum distance fails, along with conditions for exponential decay. Using algebraic-geometric codes from the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower, it constructs random binary codes with rates approaching ε² whose distance matches the leading coefficient of the Gilbert-Varshamov bound at low rates, with polynomial-time encoding and unique decoding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine one inner code with subcodes of Garcia-Stichtenoth algebraic-geometry codes, reporting a low-rate GV-matching distance bound with exponential failure probability.

entry.title: Speeding up distributed variational quantum computing over wireless networks by designing incentives for quantum processors
entry.summary: Accelerating Distributed Variational Quantum Computing over Wireless Networks with Incentive Mechanism Design arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper addresses the low willingness of quantum processors to take part in distributed variational quantum computing (DVQC). It proposes a two-stage incentive framework: first, it jointly optimizes subcircuit parameters, noise measurements and transmit power to reduce processor energy cost; second, it selects a subset of processors to maximize aggregator-side system utility. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 show performance comparable to centralized quantum computing and better energy efficiency and system utility than baseline schemes.

entry.title: Two-stage secret sharing: distributing shares when a secret is revealed in parts
entry.summary: Two-Stage Secret Sharing arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper gives an information-theoretic model of two-stage secret sharing, for secrets that become available in parts. Shares for the first part are distributed before the rest is known, and shares for new participants are distributed later without updating earlier shares. The authors define and characterize two-stage access structures, derive a universal lower bound on the first-stage information the dealer must retain, and give a construction that meets this bound. Advance sharing is presented as a special case, with its own characterization and construction.

entry.title: Reaching Majority Consensus in h-Majority Opinion Dynamics via First-Repetition Rules (Paper)
entry.summary: Plurality Consensus for h-Majority via First-Repetition Rules arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies h-Majority dynamics, in which n agents holding one of k opinions each round sample h agents and adopt the most frequent opinion among them. The authors show that for any h≥3, if the initial majority's bias is large enough, consensus on the initially most frequent opinion is reached with high probability within O((1+n/(h²M₀)) log n) rounds. The central tool is a comparison principle showing that, among symmetric rules, plurality maximizes the gap between the most frequent opinion and any competitor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use a comparison principle to reduce one round of h-Majority to DejaVu, obtaining an O((1+n/(h^2 M_0)) log n) consensus time bound under a bias condition.

entry.title: Closed-form Gaussian projections for embedded hypercube Beta-Gaussian mixtures
entry.summary: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection for Embedded Hypercubes and Beta--Gaussian Mixtures arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper derives closed-form Gaussian information projections for Beta-Gaussian distributions whose tangential parts live on affine embedded hypercubes and whose normal parts are Gaussian. The optimal Gaussian is uniquely determined by moment matching, and its minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence depends only on the intrinsic Beta parameters. The construction is extended to mixtures over finite pure embedded cubical complexes, and joint convexity of the divergence yields an explicit upper bound on the approximation error.

entry.title: NVIDIA Vera CPU microarchitecture comparison with Grace, AMD Turin, and Intel Granite Rapids
entry.summary: NVIDIA Vera: A Microarchitecture-Level Comparison with Grace, Turin, and Granite Rapids arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper compares NVIDIA's Vera data-center CPU, which includes its first custom core design Olympus, with AMD Turin and Intel Granite Rapids, using NVIDIA Grace as a baseline. The evaluation moves from microbenchmarks through NAS kernels and miniapps to single-socket performance of scientific codes. Vera achieves the best performance in most tested codes, which the authors attribute mainly to high memory bandwidth, effective Spatial Multithreading, and a low-latency memory subsystem. Its floating-point performance trails Intel and AMD in a few compute-bound workloads.

entry.title: Sensor participation in distributed detection when a fixed Boolean fusion rule is required
entry.summary: Rule-Sensitive Sensor Participation in Distributed Detection with Prescribed Boolean Fusion Rules arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies distributed binary detection where the fusion node must apply a prescribed Boolean decision rule. Under conditionally independent Bernoulli observations, it derives a signed-influence path identity valid for any Boolean rule, which reduces to an exact Russo-Margulis representation for monotone rules. This yields rule-sensitive necessary conditions for a target Bayes error and an influence-weighted Kullback-Leibler feasibility bound. The authors also derive lower bounds on the number of sensors that must participate, and numerical and Monte Carlo results illustrate the bounds and the performance penalty of keeping a fixed fusion rule instead of optimal likelihood-ratio fusion.

entry.title: Routing vehicles to improve city sensing coverage while keeping detours near equilibrium
entry.summary: Coverage-Aware Routing with Approximate Equilibrium Guarantees for Location-Diversity Vehicular Crowdsensing arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses vehicular crowdsensing, where traffic concentrates on few roads and much of a city's network goes unsensed. The authors propose a two-stage method: a non-cooperative game with diversity-weighted rewards sets each vehicle's equilibrium deviation, then the platform recommends feasible routes within a tolerance of that value that improve coverage. Experiments on London and Monaco road networks report the router reaching about 99% of the optimal coverage-penalty reduction on small instances.

entry.title: Worst-case online algorithm performance under input subsampling
entry.summary: Beyond Worst-Case Online Algorithms via Input Subsampling arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper examines whether classical competitive ratios still hold when both an online algorithm and the offline optimum are evaluated on the same subsampled input. It studies prophet inequalities and ski-rental, two canonical online problems. For any single sampling rate, the classical worst-case ratios remain unchanged, so the paper asks whether one adversarial input can stay worst-case at two different rates simultaneously. The results show that instances worst-case at one rate need not remain hard at two rates at once.

entry.title: Optimizing Finite-Alphabet Message Passing Decoding for Fully Node-Parallel 5G LDPC Decoders
entry.summary: Optimization of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding on Fully Node-Parallel Architectures for 5G LDPC Codes arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a new way to design lookup tables for the min-RCQ LDPC decoding algorithm, using Bayesian optimization over a subspace of the design space with frame error rate as the loss. The method needs no channel or modulation knowledge and works for irregular LDPC codes with puncturing and shortening. It produces iteration-agnostic tables usable in every iteration, suiting fully node-parallel decoder architectures. The authors report 38.6% better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum decoder with no loss in error correction performance.

entry.title: Empirical square-root law for degree discrepancy in binary m-sequences
entry.summary: An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies primitive binary LFSR sequences of period 2^k−1 and the range of total-variation degree discrepancy over all starting offsets for windows of length r. Computed profiles for k≤28 suggest the maximum scales as Θ(√N) with N=2^k, and the authors conjecture this square-root law. The tabulated peaks are grid maxima and thus lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum.

entry.title: A parallel greedy method for finding maximal b-matchings in hypergraphs
entry.summary: A Parallel Greedy Algorithm for Maximal b-Matching in Hypergraphs arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a parallel batch-voting algorithm for computing maximal b-matchings in hypergraphs. For a fixed edge order it is deterministic and returns the same result as the sequential greedy algorithm. The authors analyze its expected work and depth under random priority orders, implement it in CUDA, and test it on real-world hypergraphs, where it runs up to 19.07 times faster than the existing greedy method when b = 5.

entry.title: The Golden Ratio: Fair Splitting of Goods with EF1 and Ordinal MMS
entry.summary: The Golden Ratio: EF1 and Ordinal-MMS for Additive Goods arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how to fairly divide goods among agents. For additive valuations, it proves that a complete allocation always exists that is both envy-free up to one good (EF1) and satisfies 1-out-of-⌊φn⌋ ordinal maximin share (MMS), where φ is the golden ratio. For bivalued valuations, where each agent has two non-negative values per good, it obtains a complete allocation that is both EFX and satisfies 1-out-of-⌈(7n-1)/6⌉ MMS. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove EF1 plus 1-out-of-floor(phi n) MMS for additive goods, improving prior bounds, and an EFX plus MMS result for bivalued valuations.

entry.title: Rateless coding for efficient model broadcast in federated learning
entry.summary: Rateless Coding for Efficient Model Broadcast in Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses model broadcast in federated learning over wireless channels, where large models and unreliable channels create challenges. The authors propose a joint source-channel coding scheme based on rateless coding to improve downlink broadcast robustness and efficiency. They perform a convergence analysis of federated learning to guide the rateless code and quantization design, and use clients' local models as conditional prior information to aid decoding and reduce transmission cost. Simulations show improved downlink broadcast efficiency with training accuracy comparable for both homogeneous and heterogeneous data distributions.

entry.title: VR-Net: Coordinated Beamforming Across Cells for Large Antenna Arrays Near the User
entry.summary: VR-Net: Subarray-Level Inter-Cell Coordination for Multi-Cell XL-MIMO under Near-Field Spatial Non-Stationarity arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes VR-Net, a method for multi-cell extremely large-scale MIMO systems where users are only visible to parts of each antenna array due to near-field effects. It uses each user's visibility region to coordinate beamforming at the subarray level, identifying overlapping regions with a conflict graph and restricting beam design and channel feedback to relevant subarray blocks. In simulations based on a 3GPP near-field urban channel model, VR-Net keeps at least 99.6% of the full-aperture sum rate at a 30 dB threshold while uploading 10–39% fewer complex CSI entries.

entry.title: MetaCom: Meta-learned codebooks for robust vehicle communication
entry.summary: MetaCom: Meta Codebook Learning for Robust V2X Semantic Communications arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses collaborative perception in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks, where bandwidth is limited and channels are impaired. It proposes MetaCom, a digital semantic communication framework built on a Differentiable Quantized Semantic Communications module trained with Gumbel-Softmax relaxation and a Bi-Level Meta-Evolution Mechanism that treats manifold drift as rapid adaptation tasks. The method is evaluated under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. The authors report better trade-offs between perception precision and communication overhead, with significant gains over state-of-the-art methods at low SNR.

entry.title: Multimodal semantic communication that splits shared and unique features
entry.summary: Multimodal Semantic Communication using Shared and Unique Representation Decomposition arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal semantic communication that encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space. Each representation is decomposed into shared and modality-specific components, with shared parts sent as codebook indices and modality-specific parts sent in analog form. On image-text pairs over AWGN and EVA channels, the framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding and several representative SemCom systems.

entry.title: MoE Pretraining: Parallel Layout Changes the Model, Not Its Quality
entry.summary: MoE Pretraining:Parallelism Layout Changes the Model, Not Quality arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how the parallelism layout used to train large Mixture-of-Experts language models affects the result. The authors pretrained small MoE models under nine data- and expert-parallel layouts across 80 runs and compared the differences with those from changing only the random seed. They find that the layout leaves model quality unchanged but substantially changes the model's predictions and routing decisions, mainly because the router is sensitive to near-tied experts.

entry.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Exponent 1.5 in the Low-bandwidth Model
entry.summary: Sparse Matrix Multiplication Exponent 1.5 in the Low-bandwidth Model arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies sparse matrix multiplication in the low-bandwidth model, where n computers each send and receive one O(log n)-bit message per round. The input matrices have at most d nonzero entries per row and column, and the goal is to compute a sparse part of their product. For the supported setting, where the sparsity structure is known in advance, the authors give a deterministic algorithm running in O(d^{3/2}) rounds. This improves previous bounds over fields and semirings.

entry.title: Beamforming methods for massive MIMO in O-RAN networks
entry.summary: Hybrid Precoding and Combining for O-RAN Massive MIMO Systems arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive MIMO system in an O-RAN architecture, with hybrid designs at both users and each base station radio unit. It formulates a sum-rate maximization problem under transmit power, unit-modulus, and fronthaul link capacity constraints. The method combines gradient descent for analog beamformers and the Lagrange multiplier method for digital precoders. Simulation results show better performance than existing benchmark schemes at moderate computational complexity, without eigenvalue or singular value decompositions.

entry.title: Low-complexity WMMSE method for cell-free massive MIMO with limited-capacity fronthaul links
entry.summary: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO systems whose fronthaul links have finite capacity. Access points are optimized sequentially, with each subproblem solved via Lagrangian duality using closed-form updates, to jointly design beamforming and fronthaul compression. The framework is also extended to hybrid analog-digital beamforming. Numerical results show performance nearly identical to the conventional WMMSE while reducing runtime by over 99%.

entry.title: Transferring GPU Implementation Crossovers Across Architectures via Instruction-Aware Modeling: A Study of a Discontinuous Galerkin Operator on GB200, H100, and A100
entry.summary: Instruction-Aware Transfer of GPU Implementation Crossovers: a Tensor-Product Discontinuous Galerkin Operator on GB200, H100, and A100 arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper compares up to six FP64 GPU implementations of a tensor-product discontinuous Galerkin operator at polynomial orders p = 7 to 1023 on GB200, H100, and A100 GPUs. It proposes pricing each issued instruction at its architecture-dependent cost in the FP64 budget, and evaluates transfer with a leave-one-GPU-out retrospective test. The model reproduces the crossover behavior for high orders but does not resolve the fastest fused path at production-relevant orders.

entry.title: Scaling VLA model serving under real-time robot execution limits
entry.summary: Scaling VLA Serving Under Robotic Execution Constraints arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents XInfer, a VLA (vision-language-action) model serving system already deployed in production to support hundreds of real-world robots. It coordinates heterogeneous VLA computation with the response needs of robotic execution, using computational parallelism while managing interference to improve GPU efficiency and protect time-critical feedback. Evaluated on three VLA models with production-derived workloads, XInfer achieves 1.26 to 3.75 times the effective robot capacity of state-of-the-art systems under physical-execution constraints.

entry.title: FIRE: Keeping Production-Connected Experiments Reliable at Large Scale
entry.summary: FIRE: Failure Isolation and Reliability for Production-Connected Experiments at Scale arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper describes how a large recommendation serving system runs production-connected experiments, which receive recorded production requests while some downstream calls reach real production dependencies. The platform uses three guardrails: isolated tiers that redirect replay traffic away from shared dependencies, dependency monitors that terminate experiments after sustained violations, and traffic pinning that limits experimental calls to a designated subset of downstream workers. The isolated ranking tiers process billions of replayed requests per day using under 1% of the corresponding serving capacity.

entry.title: Explicit subspace evasive sets built from subspace designs
entry.summary: Explicit Subspace Evasive Sets via Subspace Designs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies subspace evasive sets over finite fields, where a set meets every affine subspace of dimension at most r in at most c points. For constant r and 1/ε, it gives an explicit construction with intersection bound O(min(r·log(r/ε)/ε, r²/ε)), improving on earlier explicit constructions whose c grows exponentially in r. The approach composes subspace design codes with a suitably chosen local subspace evasive set. As a consequence, the authors obtain the first explicit (strongly) capacity-achieving list-recoverable code with nearly optimal list size. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine subspace design codes with a local subspace evasive set, giving an explicit construction with improved intersection bound and a near-optimal list-recoverable code corollary.

entry.title: SubGPU Pipelining: Fine-grained GPU-internal parallelism for faster LLM inference
entry.summary: SubGPU Pipelining: Intra-GPU Fine-Grained Spatial Parallelism for LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes SubGPU Pipelining, which splits an LLM operator graph into ordered segments mapped to disjoint streaming-multiprocessor pools on one GPU, streaming microbatches through these stages. The authors evaluate it on the GPT-OSS 120B workload with 32-GPU B200 settings, using both an analytical simulator and silicon experiments on one B200 GPU. Simulation reports up to 2.2x higher per-user throughput than temporal execution at matched per-GPU throughput. Hardware tests show DRAM read-plus-write throughput rising from 71.8% to 83.6% of peak and a 10.33% reduction in 36-layer decoder iteration time.

entry.title: Improving bounds on hash and trifferent codes
entry.summary: Improving the Trifference Lower Bound via Non-Perfect Hashing arXiv · Nov 8, 2026The paper improves probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect q-hashing it proves R_q > B_q for all q ≥ 3, and for non-perfect hashing it proves R_{q,3} > B_{q,3} + 1/250000 for all q ≥ 4. The case q = 9 combined with the Tetra code strictly improves the Körner-Marton lower bound for trifferent codes. The method is also extended to (p,2,3)-list recovery. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve probabilistic bounds for hash and list-recoverable codes, proving strict gains over known rates for several parameter regimes, including trifferent codes.

entry.title: Random feature policy iteration for inverse mean field games with complex geometry and high dimensions
entry.summary: Random feature policy iteration for inverse mean field games with complex geometry and high dimensions arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes a random feature policy iteration method that reconstructs the obstacle function in a mean-field game from observations of its value function. The method splits the coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse problem solves, using linear least-squares fits to minimize residuals at collocation points. Numerical experiments with smooth and discontinuous obstacles, a domain with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate its accuracy and flexibility.

entry.title: Joint channel estimation and data detection for AFDM without pilot guard symbols
entry.summary: Message-Passing-Based Bayesian Joint Channel Estimation and Data Detection for Pilot-Guard-Free AFDM arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) over doubly dispersive channels. It proposes a transmission scheme in which pilots are uniformly interleaved among data symbols without dedicated guard symbols, reducing overhead. A Bayesian receiver performs joint channel estimation and data detection, explicitly modeling the coupling between pilots and data.

entry.title: The Price of Anarchy in Markets for Lemons: a study of how much trade gain is lost in equilibrium under interdependent valuations.
entry.summary: The Price of Anarchy in Markets for Lemons arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies the worst-case equilibrium gains from trade in simple bilateral trade mechanisms where buyers and sellers' valuations are interdependent. Proposed prices can reveal the proposer's private information, so equilibria lose gains both from screening inefficiency and adverse selection. The authors identify broad conditions under which sequential equilibria still achieve a constant fraction of first-best gains from trade, highlighting rare pessimistic seller and optimistic buyer signals. The results apply to seller-proposer, buyer-proposer, and random-proposer mechanisms.

entry.title: ComBO: A community-based Bayesian optimization method for switching off carriers in HAPS-Hypercell networks
entry.summary: ComBO: Community Bayesian Optimization for Carrier Shutdown in HAPS-Hypercell Networks arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies carrier shutdown in networks assisted by high-altitude platform stations (HAPS) and Hypercells, using network-wide information to optimize which coverage macro cells and capacity cells are switched off. The authors propose ComBO, which builds a graph from user reference signal power reports to find groups of closely linked cells and splits the problem into smaller subproblems solved with trust region Bayesian optimization, followed by a final joint search. In a high-fidelity 3GPP-based system-level simulation, ComBO outperforms legacy shutdown strategies and scales beyond global Bayesian optimization. It achieves nearly 84% savings in normalized terrestrial power while preserving quality of service.

entry.title: Mapping which GPU instructions reuse the same memory data
entry.summary: Reconstructing Fine-grained Memory Reuse Structure in GPU Kernels arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper introduces Topological Distance, which labels each dynamic memory access with the smallest execution scope (thread, warp, block, or grid) containing its most recent reuse. It also presents PCDepGraph, a PC-level graph organizing these labels to represent a kernel's memory reuse structure. The tool cuVein reconstructs this graph directly from optimized binaries without sampling, generally under 10x overhead.

entry.title: Tight liquid welfare bounds for budget-constrained auctions via LP duality
entry.summary: Tight Liquid Welfare Guarantees for Auctions with Budgets arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper studies the efficiency of auctions with budget-constrained bidders and derives tight price of anarchy bounds for coarse correlated equilibria. It introduces a general framework that reduces these guarantees to finding feasible solutions to the dual of a linear program, along with a new smoothness notion for budget-constrained settings. Using this framework, the authors obtain tight liquid welfare guarantees for many auction formats and new lower bounds for the budget-free uniform price and generalized second-price auctions. ★★★★★ Notable: Proposes an LP-duality framework and a new smoothness notion for budget-constrained auctions, deriving tight PoA bounds for many formats and new lower bounds for uniform price and GSP auctions; the un

entry.title: Self-orthogonal codes built from divisible codes, under Euclidean and Hermitian inner products
entry.summary: Euclidean and Hermitian Self-Orthogonal Codes from Divisible Codes arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how self-orthogonality of linear codes relates to divisibility. The authors prove that every 4-divisible code over a field of characteristic 2 that contains the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal, and that for any prime p, every p-divisible linear code over F_{q^2} containing the all-one vector is Hermitian self-orthogonal. These criteria give simple ways to construct self-orthogonal codes, yielding new infinite families and quantum codes with good parameters. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that 4-divisible codes over F_{2^m} containing the all-one vector are Euclidean self-orthogonal, and that p-divisible codes over F_{q^2} containing the all-one vector are Hermitian s

entry.title: Second-best trade achieves half of first-best efficiency in multidimensional markets
entry.summary: Second-Best Trade Is Half Efficient in Multidimensional Markets arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proves that at least half of the first-best gains from trade can always be achieved in multidimensional two-sided markets with additive values and costs and arbitrary downward-closed feasibility constraints. The guarantee is delivered by a mechanism that is Bayesian incentive compatible, interim individually rational, and strongly budget balanced. The result extends the known tight one-half bound for single-item bilateral trade, and the proof applies the Cai–Devanur–Weinberg duality framework. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the tight one-half gains-from-trade bound to multidimensional markets with additive values and downward-closed constraints, via a new dual-based proof.

entry.title: Explicit restricted isometries with sparsity k = m^{2/3−o(1)}
entry.summary: Explicit restricted isometries with k=m²/3-o(1) arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper constructs an explicit family of real m×n restricted isometry matrices with m→∞, m/n→0, δ_k→0, and k = m^{2/3−o(1)}. It combines Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to selecting a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph whose small subsets span few edges. This vertex set is chosen using an incidence geometry result due to Zahl. The authors show that proof techniques using only entrywise absolute values of the Gram matrix face a barrier of m^{2/3}, not the conventionally assumed m^{1/2}, and that their construction meets this barrier. ★★★★ Notable: The authors break the conventional m^{1/2} barrier of Gram-entrywise-absolute-value methods, reaching m^{2/3}, and give an explicit restricted isometry construction.

entry.title: Paper showing classical tensor codes and quantum Tanner codes reach capacity on erasure channels
entry.summary: Classical Tensor Codes and Quantum Tanner Codes Achieve Capacity on Erasure Channels arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper shows that on the classical erasure channel, the tensor product of two capacity-achieving code families is also capacity-achieving under mild conditions. It further proves that duals of tensor products of independent uniform random binary linear codes achieve erasure capacity. Using these local codes, the authors construct binary quantum Tanner codes of rate at least 1-2ρ-ε, with bounded check weights, linearly growing minimum distance, and a linear-time erasure decoder whose error decays exponentially with blocklength. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove tensor products of capacity-achieving codes stay capacity-achieving on erasure channels, and build quantum Tanner codes with linear distance and exponentially decaying decoding error

entry.title: Fairly splitting LLM batch energy among requests using Shapley values
entry.summary: Scaling Shapley Energy Attribution to Large LLM Batches arXiv · Nov 10, 2026LLM serving engines batch requests, and GPUs report only total energy, so providers need a fair way to assign energy to each request for billing. This paper proposes StepSplit, which splits each inference step's energy into a shared part and a request-specific part to derive a closed-form Shapley value. It works for both static and continuous batching, with a correction for the latter. Evaluated against Shapley values from 529,513 GPU runs, StepSplit's error is far lower than token-proportional allocation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a closed-form Shapley energy split with a replay correction for continuous batching, reporting L1 errors of 0.4-6.4% against measured Shapley values from 529,513 GPU runs.

entry.title: Recursive memory for prediction and generation: a theory paper on why memory needs differ sharply between predicting and generating
entry.summary: Recursive memory for prediction and generation arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how recurrent and state-space language models compress the past into a fixed-size state. For a known hidden Markov source, about O(log(1/ε)) bits suffice to answer any question about the future to accuracy ε, because the Bayesian filter forgets rounding errors. When sampled tokens are fed back into the state, however, generating T tokens can require on the order of log(T/ε) bits, a lower bound derived from the KL chain rule. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show generating futures needs log(T/ε)-bit state versus constant-size for prediction, with a lower bound via KL chain rule, tight for two-state sources.

entry.title: Third-order asymptotics for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete sources
entry.summary: Third-Order Asymptotics for Fixed-Length Lossy Compression of Discrete Memoryless Sources arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper determines the third-order asymptotics of the logarithm of the minimum codebook size for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete memoryless sources. For every interior distortion level under an excess-distortion probability constraint, it establishes a third-order correction of (1/2)log n + O(1), where n is the blocklength. The result sharpens general bounds by Kostina and Verdú (2012). The main technical contribution is the converse for positive dispersion, proved with a multivariate weighted-strip estimate. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a tight third-order asymptotic for lossy codebook size, improving Kostina and Verdú via a reverse change of measure.

entry.title: Optimal Constant in One-Shot Channel Simulation and Strong Functional Representation
entry.summary: The Optimal Constant for One-Shot Channel Simulation and Strong Functional Representation Lemma arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proves a tight bound for one-shot channel simulation by strengthening the strong functional representation lemma. For random variables X and Y, it constructs a variable Z with I(Z;X)=H(Y|X,Z)=0 and bounds H(Y|Z) in terms of the mutual information I, showing the constant term is optimal. The paper also shows Poisson functional representation is nearly optimal up to a constant gap and gives a finite-blocklength achievability bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a tight bound for one-shot channel simulation with an optimal constant term, a notable theoretical improvement over prior strong functional representation results.

entry.title: Artificial Currency and Separate Selling: A 3-Approximation for Consumer Surplus
entry.summary: Artificial Currency and Separate Selling: A 3-Approximation for Consumer Surplus arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how to allocate indivisible items to buyers whose values are drawn independently, aiming to maximize consumer surplus after subtracting burnt payments. The authors propose artificial-currency mechanisms, giving each buyer a personalized budget of currency that has no value outside the mechanism. The better of separate selling and these mechanisms achieves a 3-approximation to optimal consumer surplus, holding at every Bayes–Nash equilibrium without equilibrium selection. Both branches are shown to be necessary, since either one alone may capture only a vanishing share of the optimum.

entry.title: New linear codes over GF(7), GF(8), GF(9) via quasi-cyclic codes and Construction X
entry.summary: New linear codes over GF(7), GF(8) and GF(9) from quasi-cyclic codes and Construction X arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper presents new linear codes over the finite fields GF(7), GF(8) and GF(9), including [88,8,64] and [90,8,65] over GF(7), [98,7,75] and [97,8,72] over GF(8), and [44,7,31] over GF(9). Each code's minimum distance exceeds the lower bound in Grassl's tables of best known linear codes by one. Four of the five are built from a quasi-cyclic code and a block-constant vector using Construction X with a repetition code. Parameters and weight counts were verified by exhaustive enumeration.

entry.title: Information-theoretic study of how clustered regulatory T cells filter IL-2 interference
entry.summary: An Information-Theoretic Perspective on Regulatory T Cell Localization as an IL-2 Interference Filter arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper treats two neighboring activation sites in lymph nodes as a molecular communication system, studying how diffusible IL-2 couples their responses. Using a three-dimensional IL-2 field coupled to T cell population dynamics, the authors find that clustered regulatory T cells reduce neighboring-site interference more than dispersed ones while largely preserving strong local responses. Information-theoretic analysis shows clustering improves discrimination between weak and strong local sources at short separation.

entry.title: Adversarial risk analysis with fully probabilistic designs
entry.summary: Adversarial risk analysis with fully probabilistic designs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper examines adversarial risk analysis (ARA), which supports decision-making against intelligent opponents and uncertain outcomes, and combines it with fully probabilistic design (FPD). FPD is a control-theory method that selects the decision distribution whose outcomes are closest to an ideal distribution. The authors use FPD to model and forecast opponents' decisions within ARA and show how to handle single- and multi-stage security games in this framework.

entry.title: Performance Portability Explained: Lessons from Speeding Up ICON Microphysics
entry.summary: Performance Portability Explained: Insights from accelerating ICON microphysics arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper examines how scientific computing codes can achieve reasonable performance on HPC hardware shaped by AI workloads without major engineering effort. The authors evaluate seven portability frameworks, spanning pragma-based, DSL, and data-centric approaches, on a microphysics kernel of the ICON climate model. Their benchmarks show that different HPC systems benefit from different combinations of optimizations. They therefore introduce a measure of framework expressivity to assess how easily each framework can customize portable implementations.

entry.title: Asymptotically good codes built from Siegel modular varieties
entry.summary: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper constructs asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For each genus g≥2 and fixed weight w≥g+1, it gives such code families in sufficiently large characteristic over a field independent of the tower level, which can be taken to be F_{p²}, along with an explicit lower bound on the asymptotic rate. It also proves that for p≥5 and 0≤w≤p+1, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists exactly of multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant.

entry.title: Energy-proportional serverless computing on single-board computer clusters
entry.summary: Energy-Proportional Serverless Computing on SBC Clusters arXiv · Nov 10, 2026Serverless computing runs code only on demand, but the underlying servers still draw power while idle, so energy use does not fall to zero with the workload. The authors exploit the statelessness of serverless functions to extend scale-to-zero from function instances to physical nodes, using a tinyFaaS-based platform on single-board computer clusters that powers idle workers off and back on under load. On a physical cluster, mean power draw fell by 39.6% on a bursty trace-based workload and by 46.7% on a sparse one, with no detectable change in median latency on the bursty workload. The cost appears in tail latency: invocations arriving while all workers are off wait about a minute for a node to boot.

entry.title: Co-design of communication and learning for pinching-antenna-assisted federated learning in heterogeneous wireless networks
entry.summary: Communication-Learning Co-Design for Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies federated learning over heterogeneous wireless networks using pinching antennas, combining a segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (SWAN) architecture with a heterogeneity-robust FL algorithm based on variance reduction and dual quantization. It proposes a two-stage SWAN-assisted downlink protocol and fairness-oriented uplink optimization for antenna positioning, bandwidth allocation, and quantization. Experiments under non-IID data and communication bottlenecks show improved convergence speed and final accuracy.

entry.title: Thermodynamic formalism for non-invariant probabilities: entropy, divergence, and channels
entry.summary: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies Borel probability measures on the symbolic space that need not be shift-invariant. It introduces ni-entropy, which extends Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy to all such measures, along with ni-pressure and an ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence. The authors also address information-theoretic topics including minimal output entropy, the Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, and information projections, and connect them to ni-pressure.

entry.title: A unified codebook for far-field and near-field XL-array systems
entry.summary: Unified Far-field and Near-field Codebook Design for XL-array Systems arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper addresses the inefficiency of conventional DFT-based Type-I codebooks and the high storage or feedback costs of existing near-field alternatives in extremely large-scale antenna array (XL-array) systems. It proposes a unified codebook for both far-field and near-field settings by expressing the near-field steering vector as a Hadamard product of an angular vector and a curvature-related vector. The legacy Type-I codebook is reused for angle quantization, with only a lightweight auxiliary curvature codebook added. Numerical results show near-optimal beamforming performance, close to the perfect-CSI upper bound, with significantly reduced feedback overhead compared with benchmark schemes.

entry.title: Scheduling multi-agent LLM workflows on cloud computing with several competing goals at once
entry.summary: Multi-Objective Scheduling of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows in Cloud Computing arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper treats the scheduling of LLM-based multi-agent workflows on cloud infrastructure as a multi-objective optimization problem that minimizes makespan and cost while maximizing resource utilization. It proposes MO-SAIC, a framework with four schedulers: NSGA-II, a weighted-sum genetic algorithm, a multi-objective HEFT variant, and a random baseline. The schedulers are evaluated from workflow, optimization, and system perspectives, with statistical significance checked using the Wilcoxon test.

entry.title: Statistical analysis of structure appearing from pure noise in generalized Procrustes alignment
entry.summary: Statistical Analysis of the Structure from Noise Phenomenon in Generalized Procrustes Problems arXiv · Nov 10, 2026In cryo-electron microscopy, very noisy observations are aligned and averaged using reference templates, which can yield output resembling the template even when the data contain only noise, a phenomenon called Einstein from noise. The paper studies template matching and averaging in the generalized orthogonal Procrustes problem. It shows that under pure Gaussian noise the mean of the aligned-and-averaged estimator shares the template's left and right singular-vector bases while its singular values may be distorted. The authors bound this distortion, give finite-sample operator-norm bounds, and specify sample sizes needed for the population mean to dominate random fluctuations.

entry.title: Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes for all block lengths
entry.summary: Euclidean Hulls of Double Cyclic Codes of Arbitrary Block Lengths arXiv · Nov 10, 2026Gao et al. previously studied Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes over Z_2, solving the case of non-separable codes with coprime lengths (gcd(r,s)=1). This paper addresses the non-coprime case (gcd(r,s)>1) and covers all possible block lengths. It gives exact generator polynomials for the hull and states the precise conditions under which a non-separable code becomes separable. These results are used to construct non-separable LCD codes, and several numerical examples are provided.

entry.title: Minimum DNA synthesis time for single-deletion correcting codes of fixed size
entry.summary: Minimum Synthesis Time for Single-Deletion Correcting Codes of Prescribed Size arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies the minimum DNA synthesis time needed for codes of a prescribed size, comparing unrestricted codes with single-deletion correcting codes. It gives finite-length lower bounds valid for any reference sequence and upper bounds built from existing q-ary differential VT codes. For certain code sizes, single-deletion correcting codes need more synthesis time than unrestricted codes, by a term proportional to ln n whose coefficient is determined.

entry.title: Closed-form Gaussian projection for simplex-based Dirichlet-Gaussian densities
entry.summary: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection for Embedded Simplices and Simplicial Mixtures arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies approximating Dirichlet-Gaussian densities on embedded simplices with Gaussian distributions. The authors derive the unique information projection onto nondegenerate ambient Gaussian densities, with closed-form optimal Gaussians and minimum divergence for any positive Dirichlet parameters. Using joint convexity of Kullback-Leibler divergence, they also give sharp upper bounds for finite Gaussian mixtures with shared weights that depend on the intrinsic simplex dimension.

entry.title: FP64 Performance and the Limits of Ozaki Emulation on HPC Systems
entry.summary: FP64 Performance and the Limits of Ozaki Emulation on HPC Systems arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper tests the industry view that low-precision tensor cores can emulate FP64 on demand, so native double precision can be deprioritized. It uses roofline profiling of representative HPC workloads to examine arithmetic-intensity and accuracy needs, and evaluates FP64 emulation via the Ozaki method. The authors conclude Ozaki emulation should be treated as an optimization for large, dense, GEMM-shaped workloads rather than a general FP64 replacement, a subset they estimate at under 10% of the HPC ecosystem.

entry.title: ARIA: An AI-powered pipeline that learns radio-channel parameter distributions from measurements
entry.summary: ARIA: An AI-Powered Radio-Channel Inference and Analysis Pipeline arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents ARIA, a pipeline that uses neural networks to learn the distributions of wireless channel parameters directly from measurement data instead of relying on pre-chosen analytical distributions. Three neural density estimators are compared, and neural spline flows perform best on every metric. The fitted distributions are fed into the NYUSIM simulator, which reproduces measured delay and angular spread medians for a 16.95 GHz indoor campaign.

entry.title: An improved (1+2e)-approximation algorithm for metric data placement
entry.summary: An Improved (1+2e)-Approximation Algorithm for Metric Data Placement arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies the metric data placement problem, which involves placing resources at sites with capacity limits and fixed installation costs to minimize total placement and access costs. The authors present a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm built on a linear programming relaxation, using multiscale metric-ball partitions and a min-cost circulation. By optimizing ball radii, they achieve an approximation factor of 1+2e (about 6.44), the best known guarantee for this problem since its introduction in 2001. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a deterministic polynomial-time 1+2e approximation for metric data placement, improving the 2001 bound via LP relaxation and a flow network.

entry.title: SHADOWPREFILL: Pre-warming the Next Model for Per-Step Model Routing in Agentic LLM Serving
entry.summary: SHADOWPREFILL: Keeping Your Next Model Warm for Per-Step Model Routing in Agentic LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents SHADOWPREFILL, a method for serving agentic LLM workloads where a router switches models at each step. Switching models discards cached context, forcing the new model to reprocess the session context before responding. SHADOWPREFILL uses spare capacity on instances to prefill the context on the model the router did not choose, so the prefix is already cached at the next switch. In experiments across five agentic benchmark suites with 24 model pairs, it reduces switch-call latency by 8.5-21.4% and routed token cost by 22.5-46.1%, while normal traffic keeps its SLO.

entry.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes: a study of when shifted subspaces cover a vector space
entry.summary: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies the largest codimension h_q(n) of a subspace of F_q^n whose cyclic shifts together cover the entire space, and characterizes when h_q(n) is at least a given value using cyclic linear codes over vector alphabets. For certain lengths (q^{km}-1)/(q^k-1), it shows that a cyclic perfect code exists exactly when gcd(m,q-1)=1, and in that case h_q equals k(m-1). It also proves that h_q(q^k+1)=k when q is even.

entry.title: Concavity of Rényi entropy and entropy power along heat flows on manifolds
entry.summary: On the Concavity of Rényi Entropy and Rényi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proves that Rényi entropy and Rényi entropy power are concave along heat flow on Euclidean space of any dimension, for Rényi orders between 1 and 2. The result is extended to complete Riemannian manifolds satisfying a suitable curvature-dimension condition, with the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian. The argument relies on functional inequalities recently developed for Tsallis entropy concavity, which the authors extend to the Riemannian setting. The paper also establishes complete monotonicity of order-2 Tsallis entropy along heat flow and derives its spectral decomposition.

entry.title: Two-tier task offloading for satellite-assisted marine networks using a hybrid Stackelberg-bargaining game
entry.summary: Two-Tier Task Offloading for Satellite-Assisted Marine Networks: A Hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining Game Approach arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies satellite-assisted marine edge computing for computation-intensive, delay-sensitive maritime applications. Underwater AUVs upload data through MASSs using NOMA, and MASSs offload workloads to a low earth orbit satellite using FDMA. The authors model AUV-MASS interaction as a Stackelberg game and MASS-satellite interaction as a bargaining game, and propose algorithms for offloading and pricing strategies. Simulations reportedly show the proposed algorithms outperform benchmark schemes.

entry.title: Reliability of Ground-Air Wireless-Powered IoT Networks
entry.summary: Reliability Analysis for Ground-Air Cooperative Wireless-Powered Internet-of-Things arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies a ground-air cooperative wireless-powered IoT network in which ground power beacons supply radio-frequency energy and UAVs act as aerial access points collecting uplink data. Energy transfer and data collection are decoupled, reducing the hardware and energy burden on the UAVs. A stochastic geometry framework models the network, and a Meta-Distribution analysis yields device-level reliability distributions. Numerical results for suburban and urban settings show how UAV altitude and annular beacon deployment affect these distributions.

entry.title: Contention resolution on a fast but unreliable channel: a randomized method for sharing a wireless link
entry.summary: Contention Resolution with a Fast-but-Fickle Channel arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies how n devices share a communication channel without central coordination, using a reliable slow channel and a faster channel that can be intermittently disabled. It presents RACE, a randomized algorithm that uses the fast channel when available and keeps progress on the slow channel during disruptions. The authors give competitive-ratio bounds for expected latency and switching cost relative to offline algorithms, along with matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Computing fair item allocations within budget limits in polynomial time
entry.summary: Computing EF1 Allocations under Budget Constraints in Polynomial Time arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies dividing indivisible items fairly among agents with budget constraints and additive valuations, requiring envy-freeness up to one item (EF1) between agents and toward a charity holding unallocated items. The authors give a polynomial-time algorithm for computing EF1 allocations under heterogeneous valuations. They also prove that detecting an EF1 violation is NP-complete and provide polynomial-time algorithms for EFX in two special valuation settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open problem by giving a polynomial-time EF1 algorithm under budget constraints, plus NP-completeness and approximation results.

entry.title: Learning Global Equilibria in Non-Concave Prospect Theory Games
entry.summary: Learning Global Equilibria in Non-Concave Prospect Theoretic Games arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies non-cooperative games in which agents behave non-rationally, modeled with prospect theory, which makes utility functions non-concave and non-convex and equilibrium computation hard. It proposes a minorization-maximization learning algorithm and proves global convergence to a potential-maximizing Nash equilibrium under a proximal Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition on the potential function. The paper also shows how the MM minorizer's structure enables distributed implementation.

entry.title: Resetting-based designated information distribution
entry.summary: Resetting-based designated information distribution arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies a network of n nodes under random gossip dynamics, where a resetting mechanism with rate β is applied to a designated subset of r nodes. In the small-β and long-time limit, the expected sum of all node values asymptotically equals n/r times the sum of the initial values of those r nodes. The authors also analyze the speed of convergence and provide an approximate high-probability confidence interval for the expected sum at finite time and finite β.

entry.title: Reference-dependent utility optimization for goal-oriented communication systems
entry.summary: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes a general resource allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them with expected utility or cumulative prospect theory. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, and α-fairness appear as exact special cases. The paper gives optimality conditions for deterministic orthogonal systems and convergence guarantees for successive convex approximation in nonorthogonal and stochastic systems. Numerical examples show how reference points, utility slopes, channel quality, and budgets shape the active users and allocation policies.

entry.title: Applying multi-stage distributed real-time system design to vehicular edge computing
entry.summary: Adapting Multi-Stage Distributed Real-Time Systems Design to Vehicular Edge Computing arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper addresses vehicular edge computing, where computation-intensive applications must access different resources in a fixed sequence, forming a multi-stage pipeline. The authors model this setting using established multi-stage distributed real-time scheduling techniques. They propose a joint mapping and scheduling heuristic that accounts for vehicle mobility and deadlines, aiming to minimize local energy use while meeting offloaded job deadlines. Simulations show it consistently outperforms a delay-composition baseline and a deadline decomposition approach.

entry.title: Dispatching MoE tokens sooner by offloading NCCL-EP communication during dual-batch overlap
entry.summary: Release Sooner, Expose Less: Offloading MoE Dispatch in NCCL-EP under Dual-Batch Overlap arXiv · Nov 9, 2026Dual-batch overlap hides mixture-of-experts communication behind another microbatch's computation, but only after dispatch send releases the GPU. The paper evaluates three configurations built on NCCL-EP (GPI, GPI-MC, and GDAKI Free Flow) that reduce the time dispatch send holds the GPU. On a GB300 NVL72 system, all three cut dispatch-send time relative to default GDAKI over most tested operating points. In disaggregated vLLM serving with DBO, they lower median TPOT by 15-25% versus default GDAKI and 16-42% versus DeepEP v1.

entry.title: Evolving Infra: Adaptive LLM Serving for AI Agents at Scale
entry.summary: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents Evolving Infra, a serving framework for large language models that adapts at runtime to the changing workloads of AI agents. It separates compute allocation from KV cache management, and uses an online planner and an agent-aware distributed KV manager to balance prefill and decode nodes and guide cache eviction and transfer.
