Tested on coding, math, and computer-use tasks with up to 256 GPUs, it reduces mean end-to-end latency and P95 time-to-first-token by up to 4.1x and 14x compared with NVIDIA's Dynamo.

entry.title: Outage and diversity limits of fluid antenna multiple access under correlated Nakagami-m fading
entry.summary: Fundamental Outage and Diversity Limits of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access Under Correlated Nakagami-m Fading arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper analyzes fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) systems under spatially correlated Nakagami-m fading, providing the first exact and asymptotically tight outage analysis. It models the joint statistics of desired and interference powers across antenna ports and derives an explicit integral expression for outage probability. The achievable diversity order is shown to depend on fading severity and the spatial correlation rank set by the finite aperture rather than on the number of ports. A Gamma-matched closed-form approximation is also introduced and validated by Monte Carlo simulations.

entry.title: Correlation-informed soft outputs to reduce BICM information loss in MIMO receivers
entry.summary: Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper shows that in MIMO bit-interleaved coded modulation, passing only per-bit soft information between detector and decoder discards correlations among bits within each transmit vector, limiting one-shot receiver performance. The authors propose COIL, a soft-output format that adds pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits, and show how to incorporate them into a belief-propagation channel decoder. In a 4x4 MIMO-OFDM evaluation, a one-shot LMMSE receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3 dB and comes within 0.8 dB of four-iteration IDD with a single detection pass.

entry.title: Optimal Black Hole Search Using Programmable Matter Particles
entry.summary: Optimal Proximity Black Hole Search with Programmable Matter arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies the Black Hole Search problem in the context of programmable matter, which consists of tiny mobile particles that can self-arrange. The black hole destroys any particle that visits it without leaving a trace. Particles move in a convex area on a triangular grid, and the goal is to identify a restricted set of vertices containing the black hole while keeping at least one particle alive. The authors present an algorithm using three two-colored particles and show it is Pareto optimal in particle and color count, and asymptotically optimal in number of epochs.

entry.title: Sample-efficient noninteractive simulation over finite alphabets
entry.summary: Polynomial Sample Complexity of Noninteractive Simulation over Finite Alphabets arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies noninteractive simulation, where two parties without communication generate outputs from independent copies of a finite correlated source. It gives a construction for arbitrary finite output alphabets showing that any simulable joint law can be approximated with a number of samples polynomial in the alphabet sizes and inverse accuracy. For a concrete biased binary source, the authors certify an explicit sample exponent below 19.

entry.title: Speeding Up Sparse Equation Solvers Using Graph Computing Accelerators
entry.summary: Accelerating Direct Sparse Solvers with Graph Computing Accelerators arXiv · Nov 9, 2026Solving large sparse linear systems by Gaussian elimination creates extra non-zero entries, so solvers use nested dissection reordering to reduce them. This paper explores using the UpDown accelerator, designed for graph and irregular algorithms, to speed up the METIS nested dissection reordering algorithm. Results from validated simulation and FPGA emulation of small UpDown systems indicate about two orders of magnitude speedup over a single CPU for METIS.

entry.title: OverlapAdvisor: Choosing Compute-Communication Overlap for Distributed MoE Serving
entry.summary: OverlapAdvisor: Modeling and Adapting Computation-Communication Overlap for Distributed MoE Serving arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper addresses mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference, which relies on All-to-All communication, where no single overlap strategy between computation and communication is best everywhere. The authors propose OverlapAdvisor, which models overlap stages at two granularities and uses a unified performance model to select a strategy for each configuration at launch time. Evaluated on four MoE models with SGLang and vLLM, it improves end-to-end throughput by up to 31.7%.

entry.title: Estimating link fading and fading shape from downlink SINR in cell-free massive MIMO
entry.summary: Joint LSFC and Nakagami-m Estimation From Downlink SINR in GZF-Precoded CF-mMIMO arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes a method to jointly estimate link-specific large-scale fading coefficients and a common Nakagami-m shape parameter from power and downlink SINR measurements in cell-free massive MIMO. A tractable SINR distribution is derived under global zero-forcing precoding, Nakagami-m fading, and fractional power control. A model-driven neural network is built to solve the resulting maximum-likelihood estimation problem. Simulations show the reconstructed SINR distributions closely match empirical ones.

entry.title: Speeding up a new LLM memory module on AWS Trainium using custom on-chip GPSIMD operators
entry.summary: Exploiting Native Hardware Heterogeneity: Custom GPSIMD Operators for Accelerating Emerging LLM Memory on AWS Trainium arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper addresses Engram, an emerging memory module in large language models that mixes irregular integer work with dense computation. The authors build a toolchain that compiles C++ custom operators for Trainium 3's GPSIMD cores and injects them into NEFF files generated from NKI kernels. Compared with a hand-optimized NKI baseline for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, two GPSIMD operators speed up n-gram hashing by 1.79× at decode, table retrieval by up to 4.95×, and the whole Engram computation by up to 1.14×.

entry.title: Bounds and constructions for optimal wide-gap frequency hopping sequences
entry.summary: Bounds and Constructions for Optimal Wide-Gap Frequency Hopping Sequences arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies wide-gap frequency hopping sequences (WGFHS), which reduce interference to received signals in frequency-hopping systems. It updates upper bounds on the minimum gaps of optimal uniform WGFHS with parameters (v,s,λ;e), where v=ks, k≥3, λ=k, and s is an odd number at least k(k-1)+1. For the cases k≤3, the authors completely prove the existence of such sequences.

entry.title: Why Kubernetes can't contain a full lazy-pulling cache, and a bounded design for model serving
entry.summary: Why Kubernetes Cannot Contain a Full Lazy-Pulling Cache: Two Impossibility Results and a Bounded, Honest Design for Model Serving arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper shows by experiment that the node-level cache used by lazy container-image pulling on Kubernetes can be neither bounded by the platform nor detected by monitoring when it fails. It proposes a design that sets a byte budget on the cache and ensures a failed cache write never causes a failed read, without changing kubelet or the container runtime interface. Results from six campaigns on AWS are reported, and the open-source implementation has been proposed upstream. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report two impossibility results for lazy-pulling caches on Kubernetes and a byte-budget design keyed to filesystem state, evaluated across six campaigns with an open-source implementation

entry.title: Fixed points of binary belief propagation: finiteness, rigidity, and topological complexity
entry.summary: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies belief propagation fixed points of binary Ising models under fixed external fields. It proves that the number of admissible complex fixed points is finite, even at degenerate parameters, and characterizes graphs whose positive response is a single smooth real line. It further shows that, when varying two vertex fields, cubic bipartite graphs can realize every genus, with the minimum vertex count growing logarithmically in the genus. The three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

entry.title: Karhunen-Loève transforms of autoregressive windows using matched symmetry groups
entry.summary: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper describes the Karhunen-Loève transform of a window from a stationary autoregressive process of any order through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework. It analyzes how this transform differs from the type-II discrete cosine transform and bounds the coding-gain loss. It also presents a fast implementation based on the matched symmetry groups.

entry.title: How hard is finding competitive prices when agents are paid to take on chores?
entry.summary: The Complexity of Computing a Competitive Equilibrium in Fisher Markets with Chores arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how computationally hard it is to find competitive equilibria in Fisher markets where divisible chores carry disutility. For linear disutilities, exact equilibrium computation is shown to be CLS-complete, even with binary earning requirements. For CES disutilities, finite-precision price computation is also CLS-complete for every fixed exponent above one. The authors additionally give a strongly polynomial exact algorithm for markets whose disutility matrix has rank at most two. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove CLS-completeness for chores Fisher market equilibrium and give a strongly polynomial algorithm for rank-two disutility matrices.

entry.title: Compressing memory-based data while keeping individual items private
entry.summary: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies compression of data sources under a privacy constraint: decoding one source symbol must reveal nothing about other symbols beyond that symbol itself. The authors show that for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet, every rate above the entropy rate can be achieved with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on source sequences whose probability tends to one. They also present non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding carries a strictly positive rate penalty. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend compatibility of private local decoding with entropy-rate compression from memoryless to stationary ergodic sources and show a strict rate penalty for non-ergodic sources.

entry.title: Sharp Rates for Recovering Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
entry.summary: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling arXiv · Nov 9, 2026Bandlimited functions, whose frequencies lie in the interval [-δ, δ], can be approximated from a finite set of sample values. The paper shows that the optimal worst-case recovery algorithm has an error decaying exponentially in the number of samples n, and it gives a sharp rate depending on n and δ. It also finds that one-sided sample data can reconstruct such functions with exponentially decaying error, and identifies the optimal rate for this case.

entry.title: Query Complexity of Envy-Free Fair Division for Cake, Chores, and Mixed Goods
entry.summary: The Query Complexity of Envy-Free Division: Cake, Chores, and Mixed Resources arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies how many queries are needed to achieve envy-free division of cake, chores, and resources with both positive and negative values. It gives a deterministic exact protocol for arbitrary nonnegative nonatomic chore costs, and Las Vegas protocols for cake and chores with polynomial expected query counts. It also shows that exact protocols generally need Ω(n²) expected queries, and that no uniform finite expected-query bound exists for mixed cake and chores.

entry.title: Joint communication and control design for center-fed pinching-antenna systems
entry.summary: Joint Design of Communication and Control in Center-Fed Pinching-Antenna Systems arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper proposes an analytical and optimization framework for jointly designing communication and control in a center-fed pinching-antenna system (C-PASS). It characterizes the coupling between data throughput and closed-loop control cost and establishes an achievable communication-control performance region. A throughput maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize digital and pinching beamforming under control-cost constraints, and solved with an alternating optimization algorithm. Numerical results show 110.2% higher frame-average throughput than conventional PASS, and up to 66.7% gain of concurrent data-control transmission over separated transmission.

entry.title: Set reconciliation with linear sketches needing only O(d) extra bits
entry.summary: Linear Set Reconciliation with O(d) Additive Redundancy arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies set reconciliation, where two parties recover the symmetric difference of their sets from short F_2-linear sketches. The authors construct a randomized sketch of length L(n,d)+O(d) plus lower-order terms, with polylogarithmic update time and near-linear decoding time. The construction encodes permuted rows with randomly scaled Pinsketch syndromes, sketches the bit array column by column, and decodes using a recursive sketch called HintSketch. ★★★★ Notable: The authors achieve L(n,d)+O(d) bits for linear set reconciliation via randomly scaled Pinsketch syndromes and column-wise hinted decoding, with stated polylog update and near-linear decoding time.

entry.title: Relief: a per-step load-balancing engine for expert-parallel MoE serving
entry.summary: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving arXiv · Nov 8, 2026In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, each layer waits for the most loaded GPU in its group, and routing shifts at every decode step. The paper introduces Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that avoids exact linear-program solving and reaches within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few integer-halving passes. The authors measure three deployments: CUDA kernels, an FPGA over PCIe, and a fixed-function block beside the accelerator. They report that the kernel alone matches or exceeds every deployable scheme in effective utilization across group sizes.

entry.title: A simpler Phase King protocol that uses predictions about faulty processes
entry.summary: A Simple Phase-King Protocol with Predictions arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies synchronous binary Byzantine agreement in a learning-augmented setting, where each process receives predictions about which processes are honest or Byzantine. The authors present a deterministic, non-authenticated Phase King protocol that combines early stopping with a prediction-aware king selection procedure. For fewer than n/3 Byzantine processes, it tolerates arbitrarily many prediction errors and terminates within O(P) rounds, using O(n²P) messages.

entry.title: Generating AWS Serverless Infrastructure from WebAssembly Component Interfaces
entry.summary: AWS Serverless Infrastructure from WebAssembly Components arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper proposes an infrastructure-from-code approach that provisions cloud resources from WebAssembly Interface Type (WIT) definitions. The authors build two interpreters: one derives S3 bucket infrastructure-as-code definitions and least-privilege IAM permissions, while the other runs the component as an AWS Lambda function and grants S3 access as capabilities. The work formulates consistency properties ensuring bucket existence and correct permissions, and shows that the technique prevents selected deployment failures that a baseline setup does not.

entry.title: Welfare in envy-free contracts: when agents have few interests
entry.summary: Welfare in Envy-free Contracts: When Agents Have Sparse Interests arXiv · Nov 8, 2026The paper studies welfare maximization under envy-free contracts, where a principal assigns tasks and offers success-based payments to heterogeneous agents with hidden effort. For unit-demand agents, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when each agent is interested in at most two tasks, but NP-hard with three. When agents may receive multiple tasks, no polynomial-time constant-factor approximation exists unless P=NP.

entry.title: Design properties of doubly-extended Reed-Solomon codes over q-ary alphabets
entry.summary: A Characterization of q-Ary 2-Designs and a 3-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies doubly extended Reed-Solomon codes with parameters [q+1,k,q-k+2]_q. It shows that for 2≤k≤q-1, the minimum-weight codewords do not form a q-ary 3-design, and extends this to every nonempty weight class with 3≤w<q+1. It also proves that each nonempty positive-weight class is a q-ary 2-design exactly when gcd(k-1,q-1)=1.

entry.title: QoS-aware energy-efficient near-field hybrid MIMO for multiuser sub-THz links using circular arrays
entry.summary: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Circular Arrays arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies a multiuser downlink near-field sub-THz system for 6G networks, where the base station uses a large uniform circular array with a hybrid massive MIMO architecture. It minimizes transmit power under quality-of-service constraints using a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization framework and a near-field polar-domain codebook. The hybrid precoder is obtained by solving a sparse approximation problem with a low-complexity SOMP algorithm. Simulations show performance close to the ideal fully digital beamfocusing scheme.

entry.title: Halley: a predictive control system for optical AI data center networks
entry.summary: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents Halley, a predictive control plane for the optical networks linking accelerators in AI data centers. It reads each resource's next state and acts before failures occur, with four components each carrying a formal guarantee. In simulations, effective goodput, the share of ideal throughput kept, rises from 65.2% to 76.5%.

entry.title: Effect of Doppler Shift on Direct-to-Cell Satellite Links: Measurements and Proposed Improvements
entry.summary: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper examines direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites that serve unmodified LTE phones from low Earth orbit, where orbital motion causes Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. The satellite can pre-compensate Doppler for only one reference point per beam, so phones elsewhere in the beam retain a residual offset, which earlier field studies report can reach 10 kHz. The authors corroborate this with measurements of Starlink transmissions, link poor handover performance to inadequate residual compensation, and propose a UE-side method based on the UE's location relative to the beam reference point and the known satellite location.

entry.title: GARDEN: GPU-accelerated method for training billion-scale graph neural networks via co-designed caching, sampling, and batching
entry.summary: GARDEN: Efficient GPU-Accelerated Billion-Scale GNN Training via Caching-Sampling-Batching Co-Design arXiv · Nov 8, 2026GARDEN is a GPU-accelerated system for training graph neural networks on billion-edge graphs. It co-designs caching, sampling, and batching to reduce costly CPU-to-GPU data transfers and inefficient memory access. On real-world billion-scale graphs, it reports end-to-end training speedups of 4.54x over DGL-UVA, 1.27x over DUCATI, and 2.97x over FastGL while maintaining convergence and accuracy.

entry.title: Iterative interference cancellation for near-field XL-MIMO networks under line-of-sight channels
entry.summary: Iterative Interference Cancellation for Near-Field XL-MIMO Networks with LoS Channels arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies signal detection and interference cancellation for near-field users in extra-large MIMO systems under line-of-sight conditions. It proposes a weighted-rate successive interference cancellation (WR-SIC) scheme that orders users using the extra spatial degrees of freedom of near-field propagation, prioritizing those with stronger channels. It also develops an iterative detection and decoding (IDD) scheme with LDPC coding. Simulations with mixed near- and far-field deployments show improved bit-error and sum-rate performance over existing schemes.

entry.title: Optimal sampling and transmission for information freshness in gossip networks
entry.summary: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper studies how a transmitter should decide when to sample a source and when to transmit updates to several receivers that also exchange information among themselves. Freshness is measured with Version Age of Information (VAoI), and the problem is formulated as an infinite-horizon average-cost Markov decision process solved by relative value iteration. The authors prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter's VAoI, and that under reliable links transmission and idling follow a VAoI-difference threshold structure. Numerical results show the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines.

entry.title: Quantum synchronizable codes with polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts
entry.summary: Quantum synchronizable codes, polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts arXiv · Nov 8, 2026Quantum synchronizable codes protect quantum information against Pauli errors and block-boundary misalignments. The paper studies the case where the code's algebraic shift differs from the physical shift, analyzing constacyclic, polycyclic and quasi-polycyclic codes. It shows that the cost of misaligned positions can be corrected as erasures and that quasi-polycyclic codes over repeated-root trinomials achieve larger dimension and distance than known synchronizable codes of the same length.

entry.title: Efficient SC-Flip decoding for polar codes using normalized decision thresholds
entry.summary: Efficient SC-Flip Decoding for Polar Codes through Decision-Boundary Normalization arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of identifying the first erroneous position in successive cancellation flip (SCF) decoding when only a few re-decoding attempts are allowed. It proposes decision-boundary normalization (DBN), which scales each decision log-likelihood ratio by the standard deviation predicted by Gaussian approximation, and a DBN-SCF decoding algorithm built on it. The method achieves better error-correction performance with limited re-decoding attempts and lower average decoding complexity than existing SCF methods at comparable performance.

entry.title: Upper limits on constant-composition codes via quantum channels
entry.summary: Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper extends a quantum-channel optimization method of Alrabiah and Guruswami to q-ary constant-composition codes. It builds explicit channel and flag constructions that recover known classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim–Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. The authors give Gram and flag formulations and show the bounds are stable under permutation transport and generalized shortening. Numerical optimization improves on known asymptotic upper bounds across all tested nonbinary parameter ranges.

entry.title: Extending DBLog incremental snapshots to remove orphan rows in CDC pipelines
entry.summary: Extending DBLog-Based Incremental Snapshots to Handle Orphan Rows in CDC Pipelines arXiv · Nov 8, 2026The paper addresses orphan rows that remain in a CDC sink but no longer exist at the source. It extends DBLog-based incremental snapshots so chunk reads can emit delete events for such keys, and adds a repair request that external processes can use to submit orphan candidates. Three modes are described, and the authors state that safety and convergence are formally verified in Isabelle/HOL and Lean 4.

entry.title: DICOMPUTE: A Framework for Cost- and Privacy-Aware Distributed AI Inference
entry.summary: DICOMPUTE: An Economic and Privacy-Aware Framework for Distributed Artificial Intelligence Inference arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper proposes DICOMPUTE, a framework in which AI inference requests are scheduled under policy constraints across privately controlled, regional, and independently operated heterogeneous computing resources rather than only centralized facilities. It introduces a full-cost comparison covering capital amortization, energy, network transfer, and trust-related expenses, and a privacy model separating data residency, transport and execution confidentiality, and verifiable accounting. The authors conclude conditionally that distributed inference suits divisible, latency-tolerant or locality-sensitive workloads, and they provide falsifiable hypotheses and a reproducible experimental design.

entry.title: Entanglement-swapping quantum key distribution over MIMO free-space optical links
entry.summary: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper analyzes a quantum communication system that uses polarization-encoded DV-QKD with entanglement swapping over MIMO free-space optical channels, aiming to extend secure range beyond a direct link. The channels are decomposed into parallel eigenchannels via singular value decomposition, and closed-form expressions for QBER and secret key rate are derived. Numerical results show that entanglement swapping keeps QBER low over longer distances than direct transmission, at the cost of lower key rate at short range, with the crossover distance growing as MIMO configurations increase.

entry.title: Benchmarking Federated Learning Frameworks on Medical Image Classification
entry.summary: Performance Benchmarking of Federated Learning Frameworks for Medical Image Classification arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper compares three federated learning frameworks, Flower, NVIDIA FLARE, and FedBioMed, using ResNet-10 on the MedNIST image classification task in a single-host containerized setup. Across 81 executions, the authors measured execution time, CPU, RAM, GPU utilization, network traffic, and final accuracy. Significant differences were found in server memory, GPU utilization, network traffic, and execution time, while no significant accuracy difference appeared within the short training schedules tested.

entry.title: Study of whether first-order learning methods converge in signaling games
entry.summary: On the Convergence of First-Order Methods in Signaling Games arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies how learning algorithms behave in Bayesian signaling games, a simple model where a Sender with private information sends a signal and a Receiver updates beliefs and responds. The authors find that standard online learning methods reliably converge to strict Perfect Bayesian Equilibria but not to non-strict ones. They show that finite signaling games have a PE that is variationally stable exactly when it is strict, which yields local convergence guarantees near such equilibria. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize variational stability of PE in signaling games as equivalent to strictness, and report convergence results plus experiments across several first-order algorithms.

entry.title: OneReel: Efficient Multi-Scene Video Generation via Scene-Structured Attention
entry.summary: OneReel: Efficient Multi-Scene Video Generation with Scene-Structured Attention arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper presents OneReel, a training-free system for generating videos with multiple scenes. It keeps full attention within each scene and limits information exchange between scenes to a bounded shared memory, reducing attention cost from quadratic to linear in the number of scenes. Across four video generation models, it reports 1.7-4.9x end-to-end speedup over dense attention and 34-37 point gains in text-following accuracy while maintaining cross-scene consistency.

entry.title: Learning-assisted beamforming optimization for hybrid XL-RIS communication systems
entry.summary: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies a downlink multi-user system in the near field that uses a hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS). It jointly optimizes the base station precoder, discrete phase shifts, and active-element gains using a discrete coordinate ascent-based alternating optimization framework. A low-complexity deep unfolding alternative is also proposed, which achieves sum-rate performance close to the alternating optimization scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime. Both schemes outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.

entry.title: A game-theory model for small farmers joining carbon farming together
entry.summary: A Cooperative Game Theoretic Model for Sustainable, Smallholder Carbon Farming arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper proposes a cooperative game-theoretic framework to study how smallholder farmers can join carbon farming through coalitions. It combines optimizing individual farmer portfolios, optimizing joint coalition portfolios, and allocating surplus using concepts such as the Shapley value and core. The authors release CarbonFARM-Bench, an expert-built dataset, and report computational experiments showing solo participation is largely infeasible while coalitions create substantial value.

entry.title: Measuring how much freedom a multi-robot team can move with and be observed
entry.summary: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper proposes a mobility information capacity framework that measures how much maneuver freedom a multi-robot system can use while its motion remains observable, defined as the mutual information between a maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation. For linear Gaussian models with feedback, it derives finite-horizon and stationary long-horizon capacity limits and converts workspace, separation, and chance constraints into maneuver covariance restrictions. An aerial-robot simulation evaluates spectral convergence, safety-aware allocation, finite-codebook identification, and fleet-size scaling.

entry.title: Robust analysis of multi-unit first-price auctions with large supply, measuring efficiency loss
entry.summary: Robust Analysis of First-Price Auctions with Large Supply arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies how efficient multi-unit first-price auctions are, where bidders have independent private values and want one unit each. It uses a smoothness framework to measure the price of anarchy when supply is large. It shows that worst-case bid distributions cannot occur in equilibrium under a mild density lower bound on values, yielding a new asymptotic lower bound of 1-Θ(ε log(1/ε)) for ε-approximate equilibria. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show worst-case bid distributions cannot arise in equilibrium under a density lower bound, yielding asymptotic tight bounds beyond the classic 1-1/e.

entry.title: Proportional Elections with Feasibility Limits and Ranked Ballots: A New Solid Coalition Rule
entry.summary: Proportionality in Elections under Feasibility Constraints and Ranked Ballots: The Solid Coalition Refinement Rule arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies elections where voters submit ranked ballots and feasibility constraints specify which sets of candidates may be selected. The authors introduce the first proportionality axiom for this general setting and extend the Solid Coalition Refinement (SCR) rule to general constraints. They show the rule satisfies the axiom exactly under matroid constraints, discuss its computational implementation and limitations for approval ballots, and provide its first empirical evaluation.

entry.title: HeteroTask: A framework for scheduling multi-variant tasks across CPU and GPU clusters
entry.summary: HeteroTask: Multi-Variant Task Scheduling and Execution on Distributed Heterogeneous Clusters arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents HeteroTask, a framework for running DAG-based applications on distributed clusters that mix CPUs and GPUs across several servers. It combines kernel-wise profiling, PEFT-based multi-variant planning, host-buffer lifetime modeling, and schedule-driven MPI execution, with Bayesian optimization used to calibrate overhead corrections. On two 8-GPU nodes, the authors report application completion time reductions of 19.7% to 72.1% compared with the StarPU implementations they tested.

entry.title: Channel estimation method for multiuser MIMO-OFDM across delay-angle and time-frequency domains
entry.summary: Cross-Domain Channel Estimation for MU-MIMO-OFDM arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper proposes a cross-domain channel estimation scheme for multiuser MIMO-OFDM systems that exploits sparsity in the delay-angle domain while remaining backward compatible. It identifies candidate delay-angle pairs by correlating observations with pilot responses, then refines coefficients from time-frequency observations. Numerical results report about 10 dB and 7 dB lower normalized mean-square error than conventional OFDM estimation for integer and fractional delay and angle indices, respectively.

entry.title: Topology and information in regularized transport on graphs: how two geometries of mass on graphs interact
entry.summary: Topology and Information in Regularized Transport on Graphs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how the information geometry of the generalized entropy F_q used for regularized transport interacts with divisor arithmetic governed by the Baker–Norine Riemann–Roch theorem and the Jacobian on finite graphs. It introduces a transport defect with proven bounds and a regularized topological gap that tends to the chip-move defect as the regularization strength goes to zero. Exact computations on 1784 divisor classes and experiments on honeycomb and Erdős–Rényi networks test the results.

entry.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model
entry.summary: Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies data deduplication algorithms from an information-theoretic perspective, focusing on data streams where repeats are approximate rather than exact. It considers two probabilistic source models in which repeated blocks are modified by a constant number of substitution edits or burst-insertion edits per block. For both models, variable-length deduplication is shown to achieve asymptotically arbitrarily large compression ratios, and multi-chunk deduplication achieves compression within a constant factor of the source entropy under mild conditions.

entry.title: A cheap way to keep two bandit players in sync, explained as a communication problem
entry.summary: An Efficient Synchronization Scheme for Distributed Bandits arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies how to synchronize two players in a distributed multi-armed bandit setting. It treats synchronization as a communication problem and analyzes the probability of synchronization error. The authors derive error exponents for the maximum-likelihood decoder using a random coding ensemble, and introduce a universal decoder that achieves the same exponents. They also apply these results to bound the regret of their synchronization scheme.

entry.title: Competition and convergence among LLMs on leaderboards
entry.summary: Strategic Competition and Convergence in LLM Leaderboards arXiv · Nov 7, 2026The paper models LLM leaderboard competition as a game in which developers allocate resources across capabilities to maximize win rate. It shows that similar production functions can produce similar capability profiles, while comparative advantage can sustain distinct ones, and that diminishing returns make the competitive frontier increasingly crowded. Using LM Arena and OpenRouter data, the authors find developers improve most where they lag competitors while retaining category-specific advantages.

entry.title: Running FP32 and FP64 units concurrently on GPUs, and mixed-precision placement in WENO reconstruction
entry.summary: Concurrent Use of FP32 and FP64 Computing Units on GPUs and Mixed-Precision Placement in WENO Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper investigates whether idle native FP64 units on NVIDIA GPUs can run alongside FP32 work, and compares precision placements for WENO-Z reconstruction. Overlap is substantial on A100 but small on GH200, GB200, and RTX 6000 Blackwell. For a one-dimensional entropy wave problem, the W32P64 placement fails to reach the design order for WENO7 and WENO9, while double-float emulation stays close to design order and gives a 2.51 to 3.94 times speedup over FP64 on RTX 6000 Blackwell.

entry.title: Fast, practical classification of HPC I/O time series for scheduling
entry.summary: Fast and Actionable Classification of HPC I/O Time Series arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper introduces SAGE, a method that splits HPC job I/O traces into short windows, learns a symbol alphabet, and clusters the resulting symbol sequences to characterize temporal I/O behavior. Evaluated on 819,771 real traces from two HPC systems, SAGE-2 lowers median intra-cluster metrics by 9.1% versus K-shape while cutting clustering time from 3.8 hours to 2 minutes. Using cluster centroids for I/O scheduling reduces I/O stretch by up to 24% compared with round-robin placement.

entry.title: Capacity of distributed linear computation: the geometry of relations
entry.summary: Capacity of Generic Symmetric Distributed Linear Computation: The Geometry of Relations arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies distributed linear computation, where several users observe linear functions of common finite-field data and send messages to a server that computes another linear function. It characterizes the generic capacity, the minimum total number of symbols sent, when coefficients are random and fixed during coding and the field size grows. The capacity curve's shape is determined by the geometry of linear relations among the observations and the demand.

entry.title: TPIC: Energy-conserving space plasma simulations on GPU supercomputers
entry.summary: TPIC: Energy-Conserving Space Plasma Simulations on GPU Supercomputers arXiv · Nov 7, 2026This paper presents TPIC, a massively parallel GPU implementation of the Energy Conserving Semi-Implicit Method for kinetic space plasma simulations. The authors extend its exact energy conservation to closed domains with conducting boundaries by deriving and canceling a spurious term in the discrete Poynting flux theorem. Across several electrostatic and electrodynamic test cases, TPIC matches analytical or reference results and conserves total energy to machine precision. On 4,096 AMD GPUs, it advances 1.9 trillion particles with 96.8% weak scaling efficiency.

entry.title: Carbon-aware client selection to cut emissions in federated learning
entry.summary: Towards Sustainable Federated Learning via Carbon-Aware Client Selection arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes CA-FCS, a carbon-aware fair client selection strategy that aims to reduce carbon emissions from model training on client devices in federated learning. It uses hourly carbon intensity and an energy model based on measurements from Google Pixel smartphones, and adds fairness so that repeatedly choosing low-carbon clients does not hurt data diversity. Experiments under mobile device availability constraints report up to 46% lower client-side emissions with competitive model accuracy.

entry.title: Nebula: Distributed Caching for Faster Language Model Responses
entry.summary: Nebula: Distributed Position-Independent Caching for LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents Nebula, a distributed serving framework for large language models that treats position-independent caching (PIC) segments as first-class objects, allowing reuse across nodes and parallel prefill. It uses optimistic accounting with event-driven updates to track cache state, and adjusts shared capacity between prefix caching and PIC using ghost-hit feedback. Across four models and four real-world RAG and agentic workloads, the authors report an average 61.4% reduction in median time to first token versus the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Breaking Symmetry Among Identical Users on Multiway Channels
entry.summary: Symmetry Breaking over Multiway Channels arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies how identical users running the same algorithm on a discrete memoryless multiway channel can break symmetry and assign themselves distinct numbers, as in leader election or resource allocation. It derives a finite-blocklength converse bound on the error probability of symmetric causal protocols. It also analyzes block coding with random names and interactive role controllers, giving their error exponents and limits.

entry.title: Universal decoder for Gaussian MIMO channels with intersymbol interference
entry.summary: Universal Decoding for Gaussian MIMO-ISI: Spherical Ensembles and Symmetric Neighborhoods arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper constructs a universal decoder for cyclic Gaussian MIMO channels with intersymbol interference and unknown channel taps and noise covariance. Codewords are drawn independently and uniformly from a sphere of fixed total energy. Under stated frequency-variation bounds, the decoder achieves the ensemble-average error exponent of informed maximum-likelihood decoding for fixed channels and for channels with growing memory.

entry.title: Anchored iterative decoding of Reed-Solomon product codes for high-rate tape storage
entry.summary: Anchored Iterative Decoding of Reed-Solomon Product Codes for High-Rate Magnetic Tape Storage arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents a decoding algorithm for a Reed-Solomon product code designed for the reliability demands of modern magnetic tape storage. For the code RS(256,224)×RS(175,173) over a binary symmetric channel, it reaches a post-decoding bit error rate of 10^-20 at a raw bit error rate of about 5.3×10^-3, while still detecting and correcting 4 of 32 dead tracks. Simplified anchor decoding and binary image analysis address miscorrections and stall patterns, and an unlimited iterative decoder is analyzed empirically for average iteration counts. A CPU implementation reaches 100-200 MB/s on a laptop core.

entry.title: A Game-Theoretic Monitor Design Against GNSS Timing Attacks in Islanded Power Grids
entry.summary: An Inspection Game for Monitor Design Against GNSS Timing Attacks in Synchronous Islanding arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies how spoofed GNSS timing can slowly shift the clocks of phasor measurement units, making an islanded generator appear synchronized while it is out of phase with the grid. The authors model the defense as a zero-sum inspection game in which the defender audits clocks periodically and the attacker drags them to an unsafe bias. Their central result equates the evidence gathered against an attack with the cost of the cheapest innocent explanation of the attacked record, which guides monitor design.

entry.title: Load balancing with split items and more bins than items: a linear-time exact method
entry.summary: Load Balancing with Item Fragmentation and More Bins than Items: Linear-Time and Exact arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies assigning items of positive integer sizes, split into integer fragments, across bins so that loads differ by at most one unit. The objective is to minimize the maximum number of distinct fragments in any bin. For the case where bins are at least as numerous as items, the authors give a simple linear-time algorithm that computes an optimal assignment. They show that an optimum always exists with at most two fragments per bin and characterize when one fragment per bin suffices. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an O(N)-time exact algorithm for the many-bins setting and prove an optimum with at most two fragments per bin, improving prior (OPT+1) approximation.

entry.title: Green500: A Cluster Qualification Journey
entry.summary: Green500: Adventure in Qualifying a Cluster arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper reports two Green500 energy-efficiency measurement campaigns, at Level 2 and Level 3, on the Kuma cluster at EPFL. It extends the analysis to a full carbon footprint assessment using the MITSI life-cycle methodology. GPU power-capping experiments show energy efficiency peaking at 450 W.

entry.title: Achieving Optimal Values Under Guaranteed Constraints
entry.summary: Attaining Optimal Values under Sure Constraints arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies finite stochastic games with hard specifications that must hold on every supported execution, including zero-probability paths. It separates three numerical questions: whether a given target can be met, whether the unspecified optimum can be attained, and what an exact value is, giving complexity results for each. It also bounds the memory needed for optimal finite implementations under arbitrary Muller hard conditions.

entry.title: Improved scheduling strategies for belief-propagation decoding of 5G NR LDPC codes
entry.summary: Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy for residual belief-propagation (RBP) decoding of LDPC codes, aiming to prevent unreliable messages from propagating. It also introduces a resource-management process for updating degree-one variable nodes in 5G New Radio (NR) LDPC decoding. Simulations show the proposed RBP-based algorithm outperforms existing RBP-based methods in early decoding iterations. The degree-one variable node resource approach significantly improves the performance of both the proposed and existing decoders on 5G NR codes.

entry.title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test: a study of whether a low-degree check along random lines still works when lines are chosen from a small set.
entry.summary: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies the derandomized version of the line-point low-degree test in the bivariate case, where lines are drawn from a small set instead of uniformly at random. The authors construct a function and a set of nearly q^{3/2} lines where the function agrees with a degree-k univariate polynomial on each line about half the time, yet is far from every low-degree bivariate polynomial. They also show that once the field size q is at least k^2/ε^{O(1)}, such counterexamples disappear and sets of size O(q/ε^{O(1)}) support a high-error analysis.

entry.title: PaB-tree: A parallel B+-tree that supports batch updates
entry.summary: PaB-tree: Parallel B+-tree with Batch Updates arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper presents PaB-tree, the first batch-parallel B+-tree with provable guarantees on work, span, and cache complexity. Its key idea is a simple invariant: node overflow and underflow repairs never touch a sibling and are always pushed to the parent. The authors report that it performs better than strong parallel and concurrent baselines on construction and batch insertion while keeping B+-tree query efficiency.

entry.title: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI
entry.summary: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper presents UniExit, a runtime that applies early-exit inference to both CNN and Transformer workloads on heterogeneous edge devices. It treats CNN blocks and Transformer layers as ordered stages and predicts the latency of reaching the next exit from runtime state to decide whether to continue or exit. Evaluated on edge and edge-cloud platforms, UniExit is reported to improve deadline satisfaction and latency-accuracy trade-offs over existing progressive inference baselines, while reducing redundant computation and energy use.

entry.title: DARIC: Distribution-Aware Recomputation for Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse
entry.summary: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents DARIC, a method for reusing key-value caches across requests in large language model inference, designed through co-design of algorithms and systems. It adaptively chooses which tokens to recompute based on empirical patterns of KV cache deviations. A lightweight architecture lets it integrate with standard inference engines with minimal overhead. Experiments across datasets and models report a 1.1 to 4.5 times speedup in time-to-first-token with negligible loss in generation quality.

entry.title: Choosing a Fair Equilibrium in Shared-Constraint Games: A Comparability View
entry.summary: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Generalized Nash equilibrium problems model self-interested agents whose costs and constraints are coupled, as in controlled allocation of a scarce shared resource. Such problems usually have many equilibria, so one must be selected, and the choice determines how the shared constraint's cost is split among agents. The paper uses comparability from social choice theory to show that the set of generalized Nash equilibria needs no inter-agent cost comparability, while the commonly used variational equilibrium implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability. It introduces the fair generalized Nash equilibrium, which optimizes a fairness metric matched to the available comparability, and gives constructive computation methods for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as the running example.

entry.title: ISER-MoE: Dynamically replicating hot experts inside the switch to balance load in expert-parallel MoE
entry.summary: ISER-MoE: Dynamic In-Switch Replication of Hot Experts for Load Balancing in Expert-Parallel arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses load imbalance in expert-parallel mixture-of-experts models, where a few hot experts overload particular GPUs. It presents ISER-MoE, built in TensorRT-LLM, which multicasts hot experts through the NVLink switch to fixed GPU groups so each byte leaves its owner once. A scheduler assigns hot experts to groups per layer. In trace replay, the scheduler removed 98-99% of the excess load, and prefill throughput for DeepSeek-V4-Pro rose 17.4% on a math benchmark and 7.2% on agentic prompts.

entry.title: DMuon: Scaling Matrix Optimizers in Data Parallelism with Topology-Aware Matrix Ownership
entry.summary: DMuon-2: Scaling Matrix Optimizers in Data Parallelism with Topology-Aware Matrix Ownership and Communication arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Matrix optimizers such as Muon update whole weight matrices, which clashes with the element- or row-wise sharding used by data-parallel training systems. DMuon is a matrix-granular optimizer runtime for PyTorch FSDP and HSDP that assigns each matrix a unique owner, which runs the Newton–Schulz iteration and update on the full matrix, with load balanced by computational cost. On up to 256 H100 GPUs across three dense LLMs and two VLA models, DMuon matches or exceeds the training throughput of FSDP2 with AdamW, reaching 1.05 times that at the median. Compared with a gather-then-replicate Muon baseline, its median throughput is 2.1 times higher.

entry.title: Prophet Secretary for Matroids and XOS Valuations: A Strict Separation at 1-1/e
entry.summary: Prophet Secretary for Matroids and XOS Valuations: A Separation at 1-1/e and a 0.6767 Guarantee for I.I.D. Weights arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies online allocation where element values are drawn independently and revealed in random order, with the goal of choosing an independent set or disjoint buyer bundles compared against the expected offline optimum. For matroids, the authors give a randomized algorithm achieving a (1-1/e+10^-6) competitive ratio with polynomial running time in the independence-oracle model. For combinatorial auctions with XOS valuations, they show 1-1/e is the optimal competitive ratio, establishing a strict separation between the two settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show matroid prophet-secretary beats 1-1/e and give a tight 1-1/e bound for XOS auctions, a notable separation result.

entry.title: Binary LCD codes built from double circulant codes over F2+uF2
entry.summary: Double circulant LCD codes over 𝔽₂₊u𝔽₂ and their related binary LCD codes arXiv · Oct 12, 2026This paper studies double circulant linear complementary dual (LCD) codes over the ring F2+uF2, where u²=0. The authors derive an explicit enumeration formula using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of x^n-1, treating the x-1 component separately. By combining Gray images with a known extension construction, they obtain a binary LCD code with parameters [29,15,7] and two inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters [45,23,9].

entry.title: Seamless reconfiguration for DAG-based Byzantine atomic broadcast in asynchronous networks
entry.summary: Seamless Reconfiguration for DAG-BFT (Technical Report) arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper proposes a seamless reconfiguration protocol for asynchronous DAG-based Byzantine atomic broadcast, which adds or removes nodes. Existing DAG-based BFT protocols assume a static set of processes, and prior reconfiguration approaches either pause the system or wait for a predetermined epoch boundary. The proposed protocol lets the DAG keep growing while membership and quorum thresholds change, without halting the system. The authors state it is the first such protocol for fully asynchronous networks.

entry.title: Inside the Trap: A Renewal Law for Prefix-Cache Collapse in LLM Agent Serving
entry.summary: Inside the Trap: A Renewal Law for Prefix-Cache Collapse in LLM Agent Serving arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies a failure mode in LLM agent serving where a traffic burst causes every follow-up turn to miss the prefix cache, leaving the backlog undrained. Registered paired tests on two engines, two GPUs and two models show the trap in burst runs and its prevention by a session cap. The authors analyse an idealized fluid FIFO model, deriving a linear renewal recursion for its cycles and a self-similar regime above the all-miss capacity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a linear renewal law for prefix-cache traps and report paired experiments on two engines and models matching 57 stuck runs, plus a session cap that releases traps.

entry.title: Optimal algorithms for matroid secretary and single-sample matroid prophet problems
entry.summary: As Easy as Rank One: Optimal Algorithms for Matroid Secretary and Single-Sample Matroid Prophet arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper resolves the strong form of the matroid secretary conjecture and the single-sample matroid prophet inequality problem, achieving competitive ratios e and 2 respectively. Both ratios are shown to be optimal, even for rank-one matroids. The secretary algorithm accepts elements of the canonical optimum independently with probability 1/e, needing only the number of elements in advance. The single-sample algorithm uses one sample per distribution and O(n^2) independence queries on a known n-element matroid. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve the strong matroid secretary conjecture with optimal ratio e and single-sample matroid prophet inequality with ratio 2, both shown optimal even for rank-one matroids.

entry.title: "The GPU Needs an Operating System": a paper on putting idle AI chip capacity to use
entry.summary: The GPU Needs an Operating System arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper observes that AI chips sit mostly idle while serving models, with math units busy only about 6-11% of the time on two large open models. The authors argue GPUs need an operating system that keeps urgent work on schedule and fills spare capacity with other useful work. They report a shipping feature recovering a quarter of a GPU and a research system running a whole model faster than vLLM for a single request. ★★★★ Notable: The authors argue GPUs need OS-style scheduling; they report measured low utilization and a single resident kernel result.

entry.title: A Gamma-mixture exact solution for statistics of definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms
entry.summary: A Gamma-Mixture Solution for Definite Noncentral Complex Gaussian Quadratic Forms arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses the long-standing problem of finding exact statistics for definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms. It derives new Gamma-mixture representations for the probability density and cumulative distribution functions of positive- and negative-definite forms, extending the analysis to a broader class of functionals. The authors also provide uniform truncation-error bounds and derive the first exact average bit error rate expression for maximal-ratio combining receivers with arbitrary branches under a positive-definite Rician correlation structure. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive Gamma-mixture representations for definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms, reduce complexity, bound truncation error, and apply them to MRC average BER.

entry.title: Optimal Contention Resolution from Samples: how few samples are needed to fairly select feasible sets
entry.summary: Optimal Contention Resolution from Samples arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies contention resolution schemes that use only a limited number of samples from underlying distributions, for k-uniform matroids under random and adversarial arrival orders. It compares their balance guarantees with the best achievable under full distributional knowledge. For a single-item constraint, one sample per element suffices for an optimal (1-1/e)-balanced scheme, while two samples are necessary and sufficient for the optimal 1/2 guarantee under adversarial arrivals. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize sample complexity for optimal contention resolution on k-uniform matroids, with tight single- and two-sample bounds for both arrival models.

entry.title: Constructing evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields
entry.summary: Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper extends the auxiliary-field method, previously used for scattered subspaces, to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. It constructs evasive subspaces of a specified dimension in sufficiently large ambient dimensions, with a threshold independent of q. These constructions yield minimal rank-metric codes, more general τ-minimal codes, and maximum h-designs with associated maximum sum-rank distance codes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the auxiliary-field method to evasive subspaces, yielding maximum-dimension constructions and optimal-length minimal rank-metric codes with stated generalized weights.

entry.title: A circuit-based lag-lead damping method for stabilizing vector approximate message passing
entry.summary: Stabilizing Vector Approximate Message Passing with Circuit-Designed Lag-Lead Damping arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is usually tuned by hand or adaptively. The authors model VAMP iterations as an electric circuit, which yields a closed-form loop gain that predicts when VAMP fails. They add a lead capacitor to suppress oscillating modes, a design that often produces negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, the proposed damping converges faster than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at lower mean iteration cost, and it converges more reliably than existing baselines on ill-conditioned multipath channels.

entry.title: Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes
entry.summary: The Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies the parameters of Schur products of certain nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes, which are linear error-correcting codes. For two such codes with designed distances within specified ranges, the authors give necessary and sufficient conditions for their Schur product not to equal the whole space. They also determine the dimensions of these products and lower bounds on their minimum distance, yielding several linear codes with best known parameters.

entry.title: Sensing-Based Communication: A non-orthogonal passive reflection scheme that adds uplink to integrated sensing and communication without extra spectrum
entry.summary: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes Sensing-based Communication, a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication mechanism first developed and tested in an optical retro-reflective system. Passive tags apply on-off keying reflection to incident downlink signals, combining the sensing and uplink channels so that uplink is added without reducing downlink rate or using extra spectrum. The receiver uses cross-correlation with successive interference cancellation, and the authors derive closed-form interference and bit error rate expressions for Gaussian signals. Experiments show SINR scales linearly with bandwidth and cross-correlation time, and theory matches simulations under OFDM-like waveforms.

entry.title: Training several AI models at once over wireless links using beamforming and device grouping.
entry.summary: Multi-Model Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Transceiver Beamforming and Device Grouping arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies uplink communication for training multiple independent machine learning models through wireless federated learning. It proposes a multi-model over-the-air (M-OTA) method that uses multi-antenna beamforming and groups devices by model assignment in each round to aggregate updates simultaneously. The transmit and receive beamforming and device grouping are jointly optimized to speed up convergence for all models. Simulations show the approach substantially outperforms conventional single-model sequential over-the-air schemes.

entry.title: ReKV: Overlapping Quantized KV Transfer and Suffix Recomputation
entry.summary: ReKV: Overlapping Quantized KV Transfer and Suffix Recomputation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses the cost of moving a prompt's key-value (KV) cache between workers in prefill-decode disaggregation before token generation. ReKV transfers a quantized prefix KV cache and one BF16 boundary state, then rebuilds the contiguous suffix while the prefix is in transit. In a synthetic benchmark on cross-node H100s, the Q8 configuration reduces 8K handoff latency by 2.36 to 3.65 times compared with BF16 transfer across the tested Qwen models.

entry.title: ResServe: Accurate, Efficient FP4 LLM Inference Using Residue Compensation
entry.summary: ResServe: Accurate and Efficient FP4 LLM Inference with Residue Compensation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents ResServe, a method that compensates for accuracy loss in FP4-quantized large language model inference by adding an FP4-quantized residue that captures information lost during quantization. It uses spare hardware capacity during decoding to compute the residue's contribution and merges results on-chip to avoid extra transfers. On NVIDIA B200, ResServe adds at most 3.4% request-latency overhead over W4A4 and reduces latency by 22.4-53.3% relative to W4A8 in the evaluated NVFP4 configurations, while improving code-generation accuracy across five models.

entry.title: Levenshtein-type bounds for (a,b)-avoiding spherical codes
entry.summary: Levenshtein-type bounds for (a,b)-avoiding spherical codes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper develops a Levenshtein-type linear programming framework for spherical codes whose inner products between distinct points avoid an interval (a,b), covering both maximal s-codes and minimal energy problems. The authors introduce signed measures that are positive definite up to a suitable degree, which yield stationary auxiliary linear programming polynomials and exact quadrature formulas. Explicit conditions for positive quadrature weights and Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients are given. Under these hypotheses, the resulting cardinality bounds are shown to be optimal within the corresponding degree restriction.

entry.title: A study of how CPU micro-architecture settings affect the speed of AI agent tasks on local hardware
entry.summary: CPU Micro-Architectural Characteristic Sensitivity Study on CPU-Side Agentic Task Latency arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines how CPU micro-architectural settings, including core frequency, uncore frequency, active physical cores, and simultaneous multithreading, affect the latency of agentic AI tasks run on the CPU. Across eight experiments on an Intel edge CPU, the authors find that P-core frequency gives the largest median latency improvement. Raising P-core frequency from 2.5 to 5.5 GHz produced speedups of 1.154x for one agent and 1.341x for eight concurrent agents. The authors also release an open source framework and dataset for repeatable CPU-side latency benchmarking.

entry.title: AutoParallel: A PyTorch-native tool that automatically plans parallel training of large models
entry.summary: AutoParallel: Composable, PyTorch-Native Automatic Parallelism for Production Training arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents AutoParallel, a PyTorch-native planner that automatically searches for ways to parallelize distributed model training. It outputs ordinary PyTorch programs and can be combined with user-written, model-specific distributed code. Tested on dense, hybrid, and mixture-of-experts models using up to 128 NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it matches or exceeds expert-written TorchTitan recipes on most configurations, with throughput gains of up to 18.3%.

entry.title: Budget Re-Planning for Grant-Free LEO Beam-Hopping Access Under Admission Control
entry.summary: Re-Planning Budgets under Admission Control in Grant-Free LEO Beam-Hopping Access arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies how reordering visits in low-Earth-orbit beam-hopping affects grant-free update delivery when each region is served once per frame. It derives the largest allowed inter-frame position change that keeps the delivery-rate loss within a set tolerance, and identifies the exact worst-case loss. In a 40-group collision example, raising the loss tolerance from zero to 1% increases the limit from 17 to 24 positions. With independent priorities, the method keeps over 90% of the priority-weighted waiting-cost reduction of unrestricted ordering.

entry.title: Dynamics-aware compression of linear systems that keeps reduced models realizable for estimation and control.
entry.summary: Dynamics Aware Past-Future Information Bottleneck arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper notes that the standard Past-Future Information Bottleneck (PF-IB) can yield compressed linear dynamical systems that lack structural consistency and cannot be realized as dynamical systems. The authors constrain the objective to a manifold of block Hankel matrices and prove this manifold is a Lie group, linking PF-IB to realization theory. The approach is demonstrated in numerical simulations.

entry.title: Eliciting Information Through Ordinal Agreement
entry.summary: Information Elicitation by Ordinal Agreement arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes a simple ordinal peer-prediction mechanism that rewards agents for pairwise agreement, measured by Kendall tau, so they truthfully compress private information into coarser ordinal reports. Under a broad class of Bayesian Stochastically Order Consistent models, including Mallows and Thurstone, the authors prove truthful reporting is stochastically dominant and strongly truthful under index-equivariant strategies. Experiments on synthetic Mallows and Thurstone data and the SUSHI preference dataset show truthful payments shifted rightward and the highest normalized sensitivity among tested baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a Kendall-tau pairwise-agreement ordinal peer-prediction mechanism, prove stochastic dominance of truthful reporting, and report experiments on synthetic and SUSHI data.

entry.title: Perfect hashing's probabilistic bound is tight only for binary alphabets
entry.summary: The probabilistic bound for perfect hashing is sharp only for binary alphabets arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies the optimal asymptotic rate R_q of perfect q-hash codes, a basic extremal problem in combinatorics, information theory, and computer science. The authors prove that R_q equals the classical probabilistic lower bound B_q if and only if q=2, so strict improvements exist for every q≥3, partly settling a conjecture of Xing and Yuan. For sufficiently large q they show an improvement of order exp(-(2+η)q) over B_q, and they establish that concatenation methods need exponentially long inner codes to reach this scale.

entry.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
entry.summary: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper determines the maximum number of common zeros in projective space for any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the size of the finite field. This proves a conjecture of Beelen, Datta and Ghorpade and yields the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof combines Green's hyperplane restriction bound with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. ★★★★ Notable: The authors determine the maximum common zeros of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials, proving a conjecture and the full weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes.

entry.title: NOMA-Assisted Coordinated Beam Hopping for VLEO Satellite Networks
entry.summary: NOMA Assisted Coordinated Beam Hopping for VLEO Satellite Communication Systems arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) assisted coordinated beam hopping scheme for very low Earth orbit (VLEO) satellite systems, where multiple satellites jointly serve ground users and a ground station. The authors model the channel with atmospheric attenuation, Doppler effects, and pointing perturbations, and propose a low-complexity decoupled algorithm for beam scheduling and power allocation. Simulations show higher sum rate, lower outage probability, and greater delivered traffic than orthogonal multiple access benchmarks.

entry.title: Uniform three-fold product expansion of algebraic-geometry codes over one fixed field
entry.summary: Uniform Three-Fold Product Expansion of Algebraic-Geometry Codes over a Fixed Field arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies product expansion for classical codes, where low-weight words decompose into sums of words supported on few lines. The authors show that one-point evaluation codes on the Garcia–Stichtenoth tower over F_729 have three-fold product expansion with a constant independent of length. This yields an explicit fixed-field family whose dual codes have rate tending to 109/130 and relative distance at least 8/65. The proof is geometric and relies on an exact generation theorem and a support-localisation argument. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct the first explicit fixed-field family with constant rate, linear distance, and three-fold product expansion, via a geometric proof reportedly formally verified in Lean 4.

entry.title: Drift-resilient interference prediction: online adaptation of an extreme-value predictor
entry.summary: Drift-Resilient Predictive Interference Management: Online Adaptation of an Extreme-Value Predictor arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses ultra-reliable low-latency communication, where interference must be predicted and resources allocated against its high conditional quantile. It proposes event-triggered adaptation for an extreme-value/kernel-density predictor: a CUSUM test detects distribution changes, after which the quantile partition is re-derived and each state is refit from bounded memory. Across several drift scenarios, it reports lower channel use and pinball loss than cumulative refitting at similar coverage, with predictor memory bounded rather than growing over time.

entry.title: Balancing redundancy and synergy in partial information decomposition
entry.summary: Between Hi-Fi and MMI: the overlap of redundancy and synergy in partial information decomposition arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies partial information decomposition (PID), which splits the information two sources carry about a target into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts. The authors parameterize the feasible segment by an overlap quantity and show that many named PID redundancy measures can be written as the largest positive part of co-information over a set of reference distributions, which orders these measures along the segment. The paper also extends the analysis to three or more sources and finds that zero overlap on all pairs at once often cannot be achieved.

entry.title: GUARDTs: Decentralized Access Control for Replicated Data Types
entry.summary: GUARDTs: Decentralized Access Control for Replicated Data Types arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents GUARDTs (Guarded Unforgeable Algebraic Replicated Data Types), which embed fine-grained permissions directly into the application data model. The approach operates without a central authority, supports dynamic policy evolution, and tolerates Byzantine replicas. The authors formally prove that GUARDTs guarantee confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Experiments show that the access control adds negligible overhead beyond the cost of Byzantine-resilient replication.

entry.title: Quantum Advantage in Certifying Graph Properties with Smaller Certificates
entry.summary: Quantum Advantage in Local Certification of Graph Properties arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies local certification, where network nodes verify global properties using certificates from an untrusted prover and communication with neighbors, with complexity measured by the maximum certificate size. Working in the distributed quantum Merlin-Arthur (dQMA) model, the authors establish unconditional exponential and polynomial quantum advantages for graph properties depending only on network topology, with complexity measured in the number of vertices n. They give a one-round dQMA protocol with O(μ log n)-qubit certificates for a fixed μ, whereas any μ-round distributed Merlin-Arthur protocol needs Ω(n/(μ log²n))-bit certificates. For graph symmetry, they present a one-round dQMA protocol with Õ(n^{5/3})-qubit certificates, improving on the known Ω(n²)-bit lower bound for one-round dMA protocols. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove unconditional exponential and polynomial quantum advantages for graph property local certification, resolving an open question of Hasegawa et al.

entry.title: xDSL-CCPP: A new code generator for atmospheric models
entry.summary: xDSL-CCPP: An alternative code generator for atmospheric modelling arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The Common Community Physics Package (CCPP) helps exchange physics packages between atmospheric models, and its core is a Python code generator that turns specifications into Fortran. This paper presents xDSL-CCPP, a replacement generator built on the MLIR and xDSL compiler frameworks. The authors report that the bespoke tooling shrank from about 15,000 to 5,000 lines of code. They argue these frameworks lower the barrier to building application-specific domain specific languages for high performance computing while keeping performance.

entry.title: Memory-Bounded Inference for a 22B Audio-Video Generator
entry.summary: Precision - Preserving Subtensor Inference for a 22B Joint Audio - Video Generator under a Fixed GPU Working Set arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents PSI, a fixed-arena runtime that runs the BF16 LTX-2.5 22B joint audio-video transformer by streaming sub-block weights and managing intermediate state separately. On an RTX A6000 across nine matched prompts, sampled transformer-process peak memory drops from 8,578 MiB to 360 MiB, while mean transformer time rises from 247.11 s to 349.00 s. The authors also report that mean endpoint error increases across the nine full-prompt cases.

entry.title: Operational Indirect Rate-Distortion Functions for Classification
entry.summary: Operational Indirect Rate-Distortion Functions for Classification Tasks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies indirect source coding for classification, where the encoder only observes a source Z while the decoder must reconstruct a semantic source X. The authors attribute the gap between theoretical indirect rate-distortion limits and learned coding schemes such as VIB and VAE to the latent representation, the DNN architecture and training loss, and whether the encoder is task-aware. They introduce four operational rate-distortion functions that account for these factors and establish a hierarchy among them. These functions are derived for a Gaussian mixture source, and numerical results on Gaussian mixtures and CIFAR-100 quantify the rate loss from each effect.

entry.title: Modular Model Checking for Threshold-Based Distributed Algorithms
entry.summary: Modular Parameterized Model Checking of Threshold-Based Distributed Algorithms arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a method for checking fault-tolerant distributed algorithms by splitting them into modules, verifying each one separately, and replacing them with a synchronous abstraction. The authors introduce a new system model combining aspects of threshold automata and global synchronization protocols, and study its expressiveness. They provide a bounded model checking procedure and a way to check the correctness of the abstraction step, and report promising experimental results on a case study.

entry.title: Quantum Communication and Phase Sensing Over a Noisy Dephasing Channel
entry.summary: Quantum Communication and Phase Sensing over a Dephasing Channel with Thermal Noise arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies transmission of coherent states over a von Mises dephasing channel with thermal noise, using a heterodyne receiver. The authors derive the symbol-error probability and a closed-form approximation, revealing an irreducible error floor caused by dephasing. They also provide closed-form bounds on the Fisher information and quantum Fisher information for estimating the channel's mean phase. The work examines when communication reliability and phase-estimation requirements can be met jointly.

entry.title: Over-the-Scene Computation: Using Designed Radar Illumination to Estimate Crowds Without Resolving Individuals
entry.summary: Over-the-Scene Computation: Illumination-Programmed Functional Sensing of Unresolvable Populations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes over-the-scene computation, in which the illumination waveform makes the scene itself perform calculations, so unresolved members of a population need not be individually detected.
